Title: WM Senibong's RM6.7bil development pipeline underpinned by AA-IS sukuk rating
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: WM Senibong Bhd's financial standing and development prospects have received a boost after its wholly-owned subsidiary, WM Senibong Capital Bhd, secured an affirmation of its AA-IS rating with a stable outlook from MARC Ratings Bhd.
The rating applies to the group's Islamic Medium-Term Notes under its Sukuk Wakalah programme of up to RM1 billion.
MARC's rating affirmation is underpinned by WM Senibong's sizeable unbilled sales of RM651.5 million and planned development launches with a combined gross development value (GDV) of RM6.7 billion, providing earnings visibility through 2030.
The group also has a strategic landbank of 1,426 acres, including about 960 acres earmarked for its upcoming Centennial ParcVista development, positioning it to benefit from Johor's ongoing economic transformation.
WM Senibong's executive director and chief executive officer Quay Chew Keong said, "The reaffirmation of the rating by MARC Ratings is a strong testament to WM Senibong's solid business fundamentals, disciplined financial management and proven track record in delivering quality developments."
He said this recognition also reinforces the group's long-term growth prospects, supported by healthy sales momentum, sustained profitability and a substantial development pipeline.
Looking ahead, Quay said WB Senibong remained optimistic about Johor's growth trajectory, driven by increasing investment inflows, the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone and enhanced cross-border connectivity through the Johor Bahru–Singapore Rapid Transit System Link.
"We believe these developments will further strengthen Johor's attractiveness as a key investment and residential destination, creating sustained demand for quality integrated townships.
"With our established presence and strategic landbank, we are well-positioned to capitalise on these opportunities and are excited to undertake our next phase of growth," Quay said.
WM Senibong is a Johor-based urban township developer specialising in large-scale premium integrated master-planned developments.

Title: PN will not sign CSA, says Takiyuddin
Article:
MELAKA: Perikatan Nasional will not negotiate or sign a Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) merely to secure constituency allocations, said its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan.
He said the agreement, initiated by Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, had sidelined PN as a coalition and opposition bloc.
Takiyuddin said the CSA was an individual decision by the MPs involved and did not represent PN's official position.
He said those involved included a Bersatu faction, former Bersatu members and the Malaysian United Democratic Alliance (Muda).
"The CSA is their own choice as MPs. The MPs involved happen to come from groups that are not actively with PN, including the Bersatu faction, former Bersatu members who had left the party, and Muda.
"Therefore, PN was not involved in the negotiations or signing," he said yesterday.
Last Thursday, six Bersatu MPs signed a CSA with the government, setting out two major institutional reforms that Putrajaya agreed to pursue in exchange for their support.
Led by Muhyiddin, the six MPs want the government to limit the prime minister's tenure and separate the roles of the Attorney-General and Public Prosecutor before the current parliamentary term ends.
In return, they agreed to support the 2027 Budget.
The government also agreed to give Bersatu MPs development allocations equivalent to those received by government MPs.
On Bersatu's decision to use its own logo in the Melaka election, Takiyuddin said the PN constitution allowed component parties to use their respective logos only with the coalition's consent.
However, he said Bersatu had neither formally notified PN nor obtained its permission.
"Under the PN constitution, member parties may use their own logos with PN's permission. Bersatu has not formally notified the coalition of its intention to use its logo. Therefore, it is doing so without permission," he said.
Asked whether Bersatu would face disciplinary action, Takiyuddin said PN would review the matter alongside other disciplinary cases involving the party.
He said the review was ongoing and no decision had been made.

Title: Malaysia's manufacturing sector returns to growth in October, PMI at 51.0
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's manufacturing sector recorded a renewed improvement in its health in October 2026, with the S&P Global Malaysia Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rising to 51.0 during the month, signalling a return to growth on the back of stronger new orders and output.
The latest reading was higher than the 49.9 recorded in September and the highest since April 2026, with the sector's health improving in four of the past five survey periods.
Economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence Maryam Baluch said the latest PMI data pointed to an improving picture for Malaysia's manufacturing sector at the start of the final quarter.
"New orders returned to growth, supported in part by stronger demand for artificial intelligence (AI)-related products and underpinned a fresh rise in output," she said in a note.
Growth in new orders was among the fastest in four-and-a-half years, reversing the brief moderation recorded in September, as manufacturers benefited from improved underlying demand, particularly from existing customers.
Baluch said firms continued to raise their staffing levels and also increased their purchasing activity for the first time in three months, as they sought to expand operating capacity.
However, supply chain pressures persisted, prompting some firms to draw on stocks of finished goods to meet sales requirements, she said.
She added that inflationary pressures also shifted up a gear, with firms citing higher transport and material costs as the main culprits.
"These cost concerns, together with uncertainty over the economic and geopolitical outlook, weighed on near-term sentiment," she said, noting that manufacturers were the least optimistic since April.
She said the latest PMI data therefore highlighted external headwinds as a key threat to the economy's current resilience.

Title: Sympathy scam: Teo urges vigilance against AI-generated fake donation appeals
Article:
KULAI: Social media users are urged to enhance their digital literacy and remain vigilant against the latest "sympathy scam", a fraudulent scheme that is becoming increasingly sophisticated by exploiting artificial intelligence (AI) technology.
Deputy Minister of Communications Teo Nie Ching said unscrupulous individuals are misusing AI advances to manipulate distressing situations and elicit public sympathy to run fake donation drives.
As such, she urged social media users to verify the authenticity of such appeals before making contributions, warning that fraudsters were taking advantage of Malaysians' generosity.
"Netizens must be digitally literate, exercise caution and always verify information before making donations. Do not allow irresponsible parties to exploit our soft spot or compassion," she told reporters after a working visit to SJKT Ladang Kulai Besar here today.
She said the misuse of AI-generated visuals was becoming increasingly concerning, with scammers creating emotionally charged content to deceive potential donors.
Teo said the ministry had also received complaints from individuals whose photographs and names were used without permission to solicit donations.
She said that according to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) statistics, social media platforms received a whopping 174,099 requests to remove scam-related posts as of Oct 15 this year, compared with 102,113 throughout last year.
Of this year's requests, 170,633 posts were removed, representing a compliance rate of about 98 per cent.
Teo said compliance was high because most fraudulent posts involved clear-cut cases of deception.
Several suspected AI-generated posts recently circulated on social media, depicting distressing scenes alongside QR codes linked to bank accounts to solicit public donations.
Social media users identified apparent inconsistencies and implausible details in the images, raising suspicions that they had been generated using AI.
Teo said MCMC took such cases seriously and would act against fraudulent content following complaints, including seeking its removal from social media platforms.
She advised individuals whose identities or photographs had been misused to lodge police reports to help authorities trace the bank account holders involved.
She also urged the public to report suspicious online activities to MCMC or the relevant authorities.
Meanwhile, Teo said RM150,000 from the Malaysian Indian Community Transformation Unit (MITRA) had been allocated to provide five 86-inch interactive smartboards and related equipment to Tamil primary schools in the Kulai district.
SJKT Kulai Besar, the district's largest Tamil primary school with 830 pupils, received two smartboards, while SJKT Ladang Kelan, SJKT Ladang Kulai Oil Palm and SJKT Sedenak received one each.
During her visit, Teo also inspected the construction of a new RM4.3 million three-storey block at SJKT Kulai Besar, funded by the Education Ministry.
The building, comprising an open hall on the ground floor and eight classrooms on the upper floors, is expected to be handed over to the school by June next year. — BERNAMA

Title: Malaysia banks ride investment-led growth, but deposit war threatens margins
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's banking sector is expected to remain supported by resilient credit demand and an investment-led economic upcycle, although intensifying deposit competition could continue to weigh on banks' net interest margins (NIM).
PublicInvest Research and CIMB Securities maintained "Overweight" calls on the sector, citing healthy loan growth and resilient fundamentals, while Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research retained its "Neutral" stance, citing limited upside from current valuations.
According to PublicInvest, system-wide loans grew 6.1 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in September 2026, driven by a 7.7 per cent expansion in business loans.
CIMB Securities said the investment upcycle was supporting stronger corporate financing demand, particularly across construction, manufacturing and working capital activities. It expects this momentum to sustain credit growth through 2027.
However, the research firm cautioned that deposit growth continued to lag lending expansion, potentially intensifying competition among banks for funding.
PublicInvest Research and CIMB Securities reported system deposit growth of 3.7 per cent YoY in September, compared with 4.2 per cent in August.
HLIB Research similarly said that stronger loan demand could push banks to offer more competitive deposit rates to maintain liquidity, delaying a meaningful recovery in NIM.
PublicInvest noted that the banking system's lending spread improved slightly to 2.35 per cent in September, following a higher average lending rate of 4.54 per cent and a marginal decline in the 12-month fixed deposit rate to 2.19 per cent.
"However, margin headwinds persist, with potential yearend deposit competition likely to exert further pressure on funding costs, limiting the scope for a meaningful NIM recovery in the financial year 2026," the research firm added.
On asset quality, all three research firms remained broadly positive, with the system gross impaired loan ratio improving to 1.42 per cent in September from 1.44 per cent in August.
Nevertheless, PublicInvest cautioned that rising household impaired loans pointed to emerging repayment pressures, particularly amid elevated living costs.
HLIB Research expects near-term asset quality risks to remain manageable through end-2026, although the outlook warrants monitoring heading into 2027.
On stock picks, PublicInvest reiterated its Outperform ratings on Maybank, CIMB Group and AMMB Holdings, while CIMB Securities favoured Public Bank, RHB Bank and Hong Leong Bank.
HLIB Research, meanwhile, favoured Public Bank for its defensive profile and resilient asset quality, maintaining its Neutral recommendation on the banking sector.

Title: Judge denies Trump admin attempt to block key Senate result
Article:
WASHINGTON: A federal judge on Sunday tossed out an extremely unusual attempt by US President Donald Trump's administration to hold up midterm election results in Alaska should the Democratic Senate candidate win.
The judge dismissed the closely watched lawsuit, saying it would be unworkable.
The Department of Justice (DOJ) had asked the court to block certification of the results if incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan loses on Tuesday, because a second candidate also named Dan Sullivan would have drawn away votes.
The legal bid, which Trump has said he ordered personally, sparked alarm, given concerns that Republicans will seek to contest losses in the midterms battle for control of Congress.
Alaska is one of the states where Democrats are aiming to flip Republican-held seats in their uphill bid to win the Senate majority.
According to Trump and the lawsuit, the Democratic candidate in Alaska, Mary Peltola, has tried to get an unfair advantage by recruiting another person named Sullivan to run and confuse voters who intended to back the incumbent Republican Senator Sullivan.
They sought to force an investigation if the Democrat wins to check how many voters who cast ballots for the second Sullivan actually meant to choose the Republican incumbent.
Such an attempt "would likely result in voter 'confusion and consequent incentive to remain away from the polls.' Such late-breaking changes to the election rules are strongly disfavored," said the ruling by Judge Sharon Gleason, an appointee of former Democratic president Barack Obama.
Peltola has denied deliberately recruiting the second Sullivan into the race.
Shortly after Gleason's ruling, the DOJ stated it plans to file an appeal.
"Alaskan voters deserve a fair election, not to be misled in an attempt to rig outcomes," the DOJ said through its rapid response account on X.
Meanwhile Trump took to his Truth Social platform to claim that "the Fake Daniel J Sullivan Jr" had disappeared, and described Democratic lawyers and activists as "CRIMINALS" abusing the law.--AFP

Title: Mi Technovation's S$104mil Singapore hub to anchor next phase of AI, EV powertrain growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mi Technovation Bhd's (MiTB) proposed S$103.9 million (RM331.8 million) acquisition of a seven-storey industrial building in Singapore is a strategic move to support the commercialisation of its intelligent electric powertrain systems and autonomous driving platforms.
Public Investment Bank (PublicInvest) views the acquisition of KHL building through its wholly owned subsidiary, Ohima International Pte Ltd, as a long-term strategic investment rather than a conventional property purchase.
It said the facility would serve as a global operational hub for MiTB's Vehicle Technologies Business Unit (VTBU), positioning the company to capitalise on anticipated demand for its next-generation mobility technologies.
Currently, there is a potential order pipeline of more than 181 powertrain units, with an average selling price (ASP) of US$40,000 per unit, alongside ongoing discussions for another 5,000 to 10,000 units, PublicInvest said in a note.
Management is targeting deliveries of 45 to 55 powertrain systems this year, with 27 units already secured year-to-date, PublicInvest said.
"VTBU is tipped to be the group's key growth driver over the next five years, and we expect significant sales orders starting next year," it said.
PublicInvest maintained its "Outperform" call on MiTB, with a sum-of-parts-based target price of RM9.45.
The proposed acquisition will provide about 10,348 sq m of gross floor area, substantially expanding the company's Singapore headquarters, which currently operates from leased premises in Queenstown with a built-up area of about 568 sq m.
VTBU also operates manufacturing and research and development (R&D) facilities in Hangzhou, Xi'an and Chongqing, China, with a combined built-up area of approximately 10,809 sq m.
The new Singapore facility will house several strategic functions, including the company's main data and computing centre, digital twin and artificial intelligence (AI) centre, product definition and strategy centre, global finance and legal centre, as well as customer experience facilities.
PublicInvest said consolidating these functions could strengthen coordination across product development, customer engagement, commercial operations and global support activities.
It added that Singapore was selected for its established position in shaping global autonomous driving standards and supportive government policies.
The acquisition will be financed through a combination of bank borrowings (74.5 per cent), proceeds from the listing of Mi Material Holding Ltd on the Singapore Exchange (24.5 per cent) and internally generated funds (1.0 per cent).
MiTB estimates incidental acquisition costs at about S$5.31 million (RM16.96 million), covering stamp duty, legal and technical due diligence expenses. These costs will be funded using proceeds from the Mi Material listing.
However, renovation and fit-out expenses have yet to be determined, pending detailed planning and cost assessments.
PublicInvest said the overall capital commitment would therefore exceed the headline purchase price after accounting for transaction expenses, applicable goods and services tax and renovation costs.
Based on MiTB's pro forma financial information, the acquisition is expected to increase the company's gearing ratio from 0.04 times to about 0.21 times, assuming bank borrowings of about RM247.2 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: South Korea to double spending on AI and chips in 2027
Article:
SEOUL: South Korea will double spending on artificial intelligence and semiconductors in 2027 to a record high of US$16 billion, President Lee Jae Myung said Monday in his annual budget speech to parliament.
The country is a tech powerhouse home to Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, two of the world's three biggest makers of memory chips – computer components in huge demand thanks to the AI boom.
"We will allocate 21.3 trillion won (US$16 billion) to semiconductors, physical AI and AI data centres, the 'three mega-projects', as well as investment in artificial intelligence, nearly double this year's amount," Lee said.
"We will make bold investments in AI and future growth engines to boost our economy's growth potential, which is the foundation of its economic strength," said Lee.
He added that the government will invest 4.7 trillion won to support "frontier AI development projects, with the aim of achieving world-leading performance for our own AI model, a national strategic asset."
The proposal was made in a speech outlining his government's spending plans for 2027.
Overall, the budget plan totals 821 trillion won, a 12.8 per cent increase from this year, making it the largest budget proposal on record.
Lee now needs parliament to pass the budget proposal, which is likely given his party's majority.
On the defence budget, the president said his government wants to see an 8.2 per cent increase from this year to 73.3 trillion won.
The government will aim to secure nuclear-powered submarines and KF-21 fighter jets, and "rapidly transform our military into a smart, elite force by establishing integrated manned and unmanned systems based on AI, robots and drones," said Lee.--AFP

Title: Melaka polls: BN targets 15,000 flags in Tangga Batu as campaign gathers pace
Article:
MELAKA: The BN election machinery in Tangga Batu is preparing to put up 15,000 flags, although the campaign's traditional flag war has yet to gather pace.
The flag installation exercise, led by the BN Youth machinery, covers four state constituencies: Sungai Udang, Klebang, Pantai Kundor and Paya Rumput.
Tangga Batu BN chairman Datuk Rais Yasin said the relatively quiet campaign, including the absence of large-scale flag displays, did not mean the party's machinery was inactive.
He said campaign materials would be put up more extensively after the nomination process, with activity expected to pick up over the following two to three days.
"Many people have been asking why there is no flag war in Melaka yet, but that is how things are here.
"We have nothing to fight over. As the chief minister, Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh, has said, we practise healthy politics without malice or incitement," he said.
He was speaking after launching the flag installation exercise by the Tangga Batu BN Youth machinery at the Tangga Batu BN operations centre in Sungai Udang last night.
Also present were Klebang BN candidate Datuk Lim Ban Hong and Pantai Kundor BN candidate Datuk Tuminah Kadi.
Rais, who is also the BN candidate for Sungai Udang, said youth participation was a key strength in driving the campaign, particularly in ensuring that party workers remained active in engaging voters at the grassroots level.
He said the party's campaign activities were also being coordinated with Friends of BN to ensure smooth preparations for the Melaka election.
The focus also included reaching out to the community and taking note of residents' complaints.
"We are reaching out to as many people as possible and taking note of the complaints raised by residents.
"If we are given the opportunity and mandate, we will ensure that these issues receive attention and are resolved," he said.
In another development, Rais said cooperation between BN and Pas campaign machinery in Tangga Batu was also going well.
This included assisting Tangga Batu Pas deputy division chief Rafie Ahmad, who is contesting the Paya Rumput state seat.
He said this was evident on nomination day, when Pas vice-president Datuk Idris Ahmad and several other party representatives accompanied him.
Similar support was also extended in other constituencies where BN candidates were contesting.
"We complement one another in mobilising the campaign machinery across the constituencies," he said.

Title: HLIB retains 'Buy' on UEM Sunrise as RM4bil industrial JV unlocks Johor landbank
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) has maintained its "Buy" recommendation on UEM Sunrise Bhd, with an unchanged target price of 92 sen, based on a 60 per cent discount to its estimated revalued net asset value (RNAV) of RM2.30.
The research house believes sustained landbank monetisation, backed by experienced development partners and stronger execution, could gradually narrow the market's discount to the group's RNAV and support a share price re-rating.
UEM Sunrise is stepping up efforts to monetise its Johor landbank through a 50:50 joint venture (JV) with AME Elite Consortium Bhd to develop a RM4 billion integrated managed industrial park in Gerbang Nusajaya, Iskandar Puteri.
The partnership involves UEM Sunrise disposing of 402.1 acres of freehold land to the JV, via Gerbang Synergy Sdn Bhd, for RM972.1 million, or RM55.50 per sq ft. The agreement was signed on Oct 30.
HLIB Research said the disposal consideration represents a 4.7 per cent premium to the land's independently assessed market value of RM928.3 million and is broadly in line with AME's valuation of RM975 million.
Although development commencement is now targeted for the end of 2027, HLIB views the partnership positively, citing the higher gross development value (GDV) of RM4 billion, up from the original RM3.6 billion, and lower execution risks through collaboration with an established industrial park developer.
"Secondly, we believe the partnership lowers execution risk for UEM Sunrise, as it would not need to incur additional costs to set up an industrial team to handle the project. At the same time, the partnership can capitalise on AME's capabilities in delivering world-class managed industrial parks and its extensive clientele base.
"Hence, despite the initial delay, we believe the overall development period could be accelerated once the project kicks off, supported by its partner's established network and strong execution capabilities," HLIB said in a note.
The project will comprise industrial facilities, ancillary commercial space, workers' accommodation and supporting infrastructure, developed in three phases over approximately 10 years.
Located within the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), the site is about 13 km from the Port of Tanjung Pelepas and 10 km from the Sultan Abu Bakar Customs, Immigration and Quarantine complex, providing connectivity to Singapore and regional supply chains.
Under the arrangement, AME will oversee project and marketing management, while UEM Sunrise will undertake the agreed earthworks and master infrastructure. The collaboration allows UEM Sunrise to tap AME's industrial development expertise and established clientele while freeing up internal resources to focus on activating other parts of its sizeable Johor landbank.
Financially, the disposal is expected to generate an estimated net gain of RM47.4 million, equivalent to 0.94 sen per share, after costs, tax and accounting adjustments. HLIB said the gain would be recognised progressively as the relevant payment and development milestones are achieved.
The transaction is also expected to lower UEM Sunrise's pro forma net gearing to 0.30 times from 0.37 times as of Dec 31, 2025.
Beyond the land disposal, the JV provides longer-term earnings potential. Based on the RM4 billion GDV, an assumed net margin of 20 per cent and a 10-year development period, the project could generate average annual net profit of about RM80 million, with RM40 million attributable to UEM Sunrise based on its 50 per cent stake. Actual contributions are expected to be lower in the initial years and will depend on sales and development progress.
HLIB trimmed its FY27 and FY28 earnings forecasts by 2.2 per cent and 3.5 per cent, respectively, reflecting the delayed project launch and lower attributable earnings under the JV structure.
RHB Research views the JV positively, given the latter's strong track record as an industrial park developer.
The partnership is expected to significantly enhance the growth prospects and overall positioning of the Gerbang Nusajaya masterplan, it said in a note.
"Nevertheless, we reduce our target price (to 77 sen from 86 sen) to reflect the prevailing market headwinds as well as concerns over the current local political landscape," the firm said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Australian home prices fall for seventh month, looming rate hike adds to pain
Article:
SYDNEY: Australian home prices fell for a seventh month in October, with the downturn proving steeper than any in the past four decades, while the heightened risk of another imminent rate hike added to more pain for a once-booming housing market.
Figures on Monday from property data firm Cotality showed national home prices fell 1.2 per cent in October from September, when they dropped by a downward revised figure of 1.3 per cent. That left values 6.7 per cent below their peak and down 2.8 per cent from a year ago.
Capital-city home values were falling at their fastest in 40 years, the firm said, with prices down 8.1 per cent in just seven months.
That surpassed a decline of 7.0 per cent over the same timeframe in 2022-2023, when the central bank raised interest rates sharply to tame inflation after the Covid-19 pandemic.
Mid-sized capitals led the declines in October, with Brisbane home values falling 2.0 per cent and Perth down 1.7 per cent, unwinding some of the gains of roughly 50 per cent racked up over the past five years.
Sydney prices fell 1.6 per cent in the month, leaving values 1.5 per cent below where they were five years ago.
"Buyers have a lot more stock to choose from, they have more leverage and there isn't the same urgency to buy as there was a year ago when home values were rising rapidly," said the firm's research director, Tim Lawless.
"But despite this being a buyer's market, they are noticeably absent, reflecting low confidence and ongoing serviceability barriers."
Property sales have slumped, falling 23 per cent from a year earlier and standing 18 per cent below the five-year average. The drop has been most pronounced in Sydney, where transaction volumes are down 30 per cent from a year ago.
Adding to more weakness ahead, the Reserve Bank of Australia is widely expected to raise interest rates a fifth time next Tuesday to 4.85 per cent, a 18-year high, to fight inflation.
Markets imply nearly a 90 per cent probability of a hike, with a 20 per cent chance that interest rates could reach 5.1 per cent.
Policymakers have flagged the housing market as a downside risk to the economy but were sanguine about any financial stability risks from a property downturn.
Most Australian mortgage holders would still be in positive equity if house prices dived 20 per cent, the RBA said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No unhealthy API readings recorded nationwide this morning
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: No areas in the country recorded unhealthy air quality as at 7.30am today.
According to the latest data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), 44 monitoring stations recorded moderate Air Pollutant Index (API) readings across 11 states and two federal territories.
The states and federal territories were Johor, Sarawak, Negri Sembilan, Pahang, Sabah, Melaka, Selangor, Perak, Penang, Kelantan, Terengganu, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.
Another 24 monitoring stations recorded good API readings.
API readings of zero to 50 are classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are considered hazardous.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecast rain in several areas of the peninsula this morning.
These include inland areas of Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and Labuan.
Rain is also expected in parts of inland Sandakan, Sabah, as well as Betong, Kapit and Mukah in Sarawak.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TSH Resources agrees to Singapore haze assessment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: TSH Resources Bhd has offered to engage assessors from a Singapore government panel at its own expense amid investigations into forest fires in Indonesia linked to transboundary haze.
The plantation group said it had written to Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) confirming its willingness to have its operations, corporate relationships and supply chains assessed.
The move follows notices issued by NEA to its two Singapore-incorporated subsidiaries, TSH Oversea Pte Ltd and TSH Global Plantation Pte Ltd, under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act 2014.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Monday, TSH said it would cooperate with the assessors in accordance with applicable laws and regulatory requirements, as well as any directions issued by NEA.
"The company shares the government's concern over the impact of the fires and haze and welcomes the opportunity to engage constructively with the relevant authorities and independent assessors," it said.
This comes after TSH said on Oct 29 that its review of available records had not identified any business relationships with 10 Indonesian companies named by NEA in connection with forest and peatland fires.
It said none of the companies was its subsidiary, associate or joint venture, nor had it identified any direct operational, supply-chain or business relationship with them.
Singapore has stepped up scrutiny of companies potentially linked to the haze, establishing a specialist panel comprising investigation firms and legal advisers to examine their operations, corporate relationships and supply chains.
The panel includes Control Risks Group, FTI Consulting (Singapore) and Kroll Singapore, alongside four law firms or legal advisers, according to Singapore media reports.
The assessors will submit their findings to NEA, which will determine whether further regulatory action is warranted.
TSH said it would provide further updates when there were material developments.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Media Innovation Fund 2.0 to boost industry competitiveness, protect jobs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Media Innovation Fund 2.0 will help strengthen the competitiveness and technological capabilities of local media companies while ensuring industry sustainability.
Malaysian Media Council (MMC) chairman Tan Sri Nallini Pathmanathan said the fund was timely as media organisations struggled to keep pace with rapid technological advancements, artificial intelligence (AI) adoption, intense competition from digital platforms, and changing news consumption habits.
Nallini supported Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil's reminder that recipient companies must not terminate employees arbitrarily.
"Amid the advancement of AI and digital technology, the media industry must continue to nurture and protect the talent and workforce that form the backbone of the industry itself.
"For instance, the work of media practitioners is being used by AI systems, yet the journalists who produce the content are not given due credit. Therefore, the human role of journalists remains crucial in delivering credible news," she said.
Meanwhile, Media Chinese International Limited (MCIL) (Malaysia) Group editor-in-chief Datuk Kuik Cheng Kang said the fund reflected the government's commitment to helping media organisations chart a new direction while protecting workers' welfare.
Kuik said mainstream media organisations were undergoing a difficult transition, as digital revenue had yet to generate sufficient returns to cover operating costs.
Substantial expenditure, he said, was required to maintain fully equipped newsrooms, professional editorial teams, and nationwide coverage networks.
"The reality is that without large-scale workforce reductions, it is extremely difficult for a media organisation to remain viable by relying solely on digital revenue. This may sound harsh, but it is the reality that media operators have to face.
"Of course, we do not want job cuts, let alone media practitioners losing their livelihoods as a result of the industry's transformation. However, if the organisations themselves fail to operate sustainably, how can the welfare of their employees continue to be protected?" he said.
Kuik suggested the government also help media companies build sustainable business models to retain top talent and produce responsible journalism.
"Times may change the way media organisations conduct business and technology may transform news channels, but society's need for truthful information, professional judgement and the media's role in providing checks and balances must never be eroded," he said.
Malaysia Tribune editor-in-chief Sharaimei Shaik Ahmedullah described the fund as an essential lifeline to reinforce digital publishing operations and upskill workers.
She said Malaysia Tribune, which benefited from the fund's first phase, used the grant to improve the operational efficiency of its news portal and make its digital platform more competitive.
"Overall, the Media Innovation Fund has the potential to help Malaysia Tribune enhance its organisational capabilities in terms of technology, human resources and content innovation, thereby strengthening its position in an increasingly competitive digital media landscape," she said.
Sharaimei also welcomed the employee retention condition, saying worker welfare must be safeguarded alongside the provision of financial assistance.
Last Friday, Fahmi announced an allocation of RM30 million under the Media Innovation Fund 2.0 to support the local media industry through digitalisation, talent development, and the adoption of emerging technologies such as AI.
The initiative builds on the original Media Innovation Fund announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in conjunction with National Journalists' Day (Hawana).
The fund covers five areas: training for media personnel; software and technology adaptation; equipment, hardware, and support facilities; content research and development; and subscriptions to news services and media content.
Applications opened yesterday and close on Nov 14 via https://danainovasimedia.komunikasi.gov.my/.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Health Ministry faces 1,176-driver shortage, including for ambulances
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry is facing a shortage of 1,176 vehicle drivers, including ambulance drivers, across its facilities nationwide.
The shortfall has increased the workload of existing drivers and is expected to persist until April next year.
The ministry attributed the shortage to delays in filling General Services Assistant (Driving) positions following the temporary suspension of recruitment by the Public Service Department (PSD) through the Public Services Commission (PSC) in 2024.
The suspension was implemented to facilitate the introduction of the new Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA).
"Under the new system, the former vehicle driver scheme has been consolidated into a new scheme known as General Services Assistant (Driving), under the Skills Services classification (H).
"The changes required a thorough review of qualification requirements to ensure recruits are suitable and competent in driving duties, particularly when operating ambulances.
"The new scheme also encourages a broader scope of duties, multi-skilling and the performance of multiple tasks," the ministry said in a response to a recent report by Berita Harian.
The ministry expects vacancies for General Services Assistant (Driving) positions at public healthcare facilities nationwide to be filled in stages from April 2027.
As at Sept 30 this year, the ministry had 8,863 approved positions for General Services Assistant (Driving), of which only 7,687 were filled.
Peninsular Malaysia recorded the highest number of vacancies at 1,003, followed by Sarawak (92), Sabah (73) and Labuan (eight).
However, the ministry said recruitment projections must take into account existing vacancies, retirements, staff attrition and the operational needs of healthcare facilities.
"Based on the status of recruitment matters with the SPA, applications to fill the vacancies are still being processed by the commission. The Driving Competency Test (UKP) was only completed on Oct 27.
"Appointments will be made in stages from April 2027, subject to the completion of the recruitment process by the PSC," it said.
The ministry said the implementation of SSPA had also necessitated a review of job functions and placements to separate overlapping duties between General Services Assistant (Driving) and General Services Assistant (General) positions.
It said existing General Services Assistants (General) could be assigned driving duties at government facilities at the discretion of state health department directors or heads of departments, subject to service requirements, driving tests and competency assessments.
"The General Services Assistant (Driving) scheme covers the functions of the former Vehicle Driver scheme before SSPA, focusing on driving duties and the maintenance of departmental vehicles, including ambulances, at their respective placement facilities.
"Meanwhile, the General Services Assistant (General) scheme focuses on general support duties based on departmental needs, including functions previously performed by Operations Assistants and Public Works Assistants before SSPA," it said.
The ministry's response followed a report on Oct 16 highlighting a shortage of ambulance drivers at government healthcare facilities nationwide, despite the procurement of 400 new ambulances announced under the 2027 Budget.

Title: Kalimaran festival celebrates Murut heritage, strengthens ties with other communities
Article:
TENOM: The Kalimaran festival celebrates the cultural heritage of Sabah's Murut community while fostering closer ties with other ethnic groups.
Sabah Rural Development Minister Datuk Rubin Balang said the festival originated from Injawari or Panawari, a traditional gathering held by the Murut community before independence during British colonial rule.
He said the celebration was later renamed Kalimaran following discussions within the association, with the new name reflecting values such as diligence, competitiveness and unity.
"The festival's long history shows that Murut cultural heritage has deep traditional roots and must be preserved as a symbol of the community's identity and pride," he said at the 20th Kalimaran festival in Kemabong near here recently.
Rubin, who is the Kemabong assemblyman and Sabah Murut Association president, said the festival provided a platform to showcase Murut customs, arts and traditional crafts while ensuring they were passed down to future generations.
[[nid:1568772]]
Since last year, the Lundayeh community has also been involved in organising the festival, broadening its scope to showcase the traditions, handicrafts and heritage of both communities.
This year's theme, "Migogondo Jumalai Sumingkot", meaning "United in Progress and Development", highlights the importance of cooperation in building a united, progressive and competitive society.
Meanwhile, Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor called on younger generations to preserve their cultural heritage and draw inspiration from Murut warrior Ontoros Endoi, better known as Antanom, whose courage and determination remain an important part of the community's history.
In his speech, delivered by Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Ewon Benedick at the festival, Hajiji said Antanom's legacy was not merely about the courage to fight, but also about dignity, self-respect, leadership, loyalty to one's homeland and love for the community.
"These values remain highly relevant in our lives today. I want the spirit of Antanom to continue inspiring Sabah's younger generation to appreciate their homeland, uphold unity, face challenges with courage, acquire knowledge and skills, develop a strong sense of identity and always contribute to the state and nation," he said.

Title: Poor nutrition puts Malaysian children's long-term health at risk
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Many children in Malaysia are facing "hidden hunger", a form of malnutrition in which they may not appear underweight or stunted, or show signs of inadequate food intake, but are still lacking essential nutrients.
The problem occurs when children consume enough food in terms of quantity, but their daily diets fail to provide the nutrients needed for physical growth, cognitive development, immunity and long-term health.
Experts warn that if left unaddressed, this could have lasting effects on children's physical and cognitive development, as well as their health into adulthood.
More concerning is that malnutrition can coexist with overweight and obesity, creating a more complex public health challenge.
Several studies reviewed by Berita Harian found that failure to address nutritional issues from an early age could affect not only children's growth and health, but also their quality of life and ability to reach their full potential.
The findings of the second South-East Asian Nutrition Surveys (SEANUTS II) Malaysia showed that 94.8 per cent of children had inadequate vitamin D intake, while 79.4 per cent did not meet the recommended calcium intake.
The survey, conducted every eight to 10 years, was last carried out in 2019 and 2020 under SEANUTS II.
More worryingly, 40.3 per cent of children below the age of four were found to be anaemic, indicating that nutritional deficiencies can occur even among children who do not appear underweight or underfed.
The research sampled 2,989 children aged 0.5 to 12.9 years, representing roughly 4.9 million children in that age group across Peninsular Malaysia.
It also found that Malaysian children face a "triple burden of malnutrition", where stunting, wasting, overweight and obesity occur within the same child population.
The survey recorded 8.9 per cent of children experiencing stunting, 6.7 per cent wasting, 9.2 per cent overweight, and 8.8 per cent obesity.
SEANUTS II Malaysia principal investigator and Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) Faculty of Health Sciences lecturer Professor Dr Poh Bee Koon said the findings showed that weight and body size alone were no longer sufficient indicators of children's nutritional status.
She said greater attention must also be given to diet quality and adequate micronutrient intake.
More concerning, she said, nutritional challenges did not end as children grew older but could persist into adolescence.
The 2022 National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) found that 30.5 per cent of Malaysian adolescents aged between 13 and 17 were overweight or obese, while 8.3 per cent were underweight and 6.8 per cent stunted.
At the same time, 83.9 per cent of adolescents did not consume sufficient fruits and vegetables, while 32.4 per cent drank carbonated beverages at least once a day.
Poh said childhood nutritional challenges have grown more complex because children can look normal or carry excess weight while subsisting on low-quality diets lacking essential nutrients.
"This means the question of children's nutrition is no longer simply whether they have enough food, but also what they eat, the nutrients it contains and their daily lifestyle habits.
"Children may appear to have a normal weight or be overweight, but still have poor diet quality or insufficient intake of essential nutrients.
"Meal timings are also an important consideration, particularly among primary schoolchildren," she said.
She said SEANUTS II analysis found that 36 per cent of primary schoolchildren skipped breakfast at least once a week.
The habit was associated with lower energy and nutrient intake, including cereals, vegetables, milk and dairy products.
Poh said this showed that children's nutritional problems were not solely related to the amount of food they consumed, but also to diet quality and regular meal patterns.
"When breakfast is skipped, some of the nutrients that should be obtained early in the day may not be fully replaced during the following meals," she said.
She said children's nutrition should also be considered alongside other factors, including physical activity, sedentary lifestyles, screen time and sleep, all of which were interconnected in shaping their overall health.

Title: OPEC+ to maintain oil output for third consecutive month in December
Article:
VIENNA: The Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and its allies, known as OPEC+, will keep their oil output levels unchanged for the third consecutive month in December, OPEC said in a statement on Sunday, reported Xinhua.
Seven OPEC+ countries, including Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman, announced the decision after a virtual meeting to review global market conditions and the outlook.
"The seven participating countries decided to maintain September 2026 required production for December 2026," the statement noted.
Under the agreement, the seven countries will maintain their combined required production level at approximately 31.01 million barrel per day (bpd) in December. Saudi Arabia's required production level will remain at 10.48 million bpd, followed by Russia at 9.95 million bpd and Iraq at 4.43 million bpd.
They had been raising oil output on a monthly basis from April to September this year. They paused the increases in October and kept November's output unchanged.
OPEC said the seven countries will hold their next meeting on Nov 29 to review market conditions.

Title: Tesla, Samsung oppose new US tariffs on Vietnam as probe deadline nears
Article:
HANOI: Businesses are divided over whether Washington should propose new tariffs on Vietnamese goods this month, with Tesla and Samsung not in favour, while others have called for penalties, submissions to the US government show.
The Trump administration has set a Nov 29 deadline to conclude a trade probe launched in May over the Southeast Asian nation's alleged intellectual property violations. It designated Vietnam as a "priority foreign country", the first jurisdiction in 13 years to be ​added to the most serious US watchlist category.
The US has accused Vietnam of "a persistent failure to resolve long-standing concerns about IP protection and enforcement." A separate probe into alleged excessive capacity is also underway. Vietnam has urged Washington to conduct its investigations objectively.
It is not clear if any tariffs linked to IP violations would be general or sector specific. The US currently levies a general 12.5 per cent tariff on Vietnamese goods that was imposed in July after an investigation into alleged failures to prevent imports of goods made with forced labour.
Vietnam, long accused of being a transit hub for Chinese goods, faced 20 per cent tariffs after Trump's "Liberation Day", which were struck down by the Supreme Court. Many economists have said the objective of the Trump administration is to reimpose at least the same level of tariffs that the Supreme Court abolished.
Electric car maker Tesla urged the US Trade Representative to "take into account the supply chain needs of American manufacturers". Some advanced components and precision manufacturing equipment cannot be sourced domestically despite major investments in US production, it said in comments sent on July 2.
Samsung's US unit made a similar argument, noting Vietnam produces a significant share of Samsung's smartphones and network equipment for the US market. The South Korean company is Vietnam's largest foreign investor, having invested about US$25 billion there.
Retail groups and trade associations representing industries with extensive manufacturing operations in Vietnam, including footwear, apparel and makers of consumer goods such as bikes or video game consoles, also opposed additional tariffs.
Vietnam's exports to US surged 42 per cent in the first eight months of this year compared to the same period in 2025, making it the US trading partner with the largest goods surplus ahead of China and Mexico. That compares with its position as the fourth-biggest at the end of 2025.
STEEL, SOLAR AND WOOD GROUPS ALLEGE UNFAIR PRACTICES
Industry groups representing US producers of steel, seafood, plywood, solar panels and wood products accused Vietnam of unfair practices and called for new tariffs.
Copyright holders such as software, film and music industry groups urged Washington to secure concrete commitments from Vietnam to combat widespread piracy.
The Business Software Alliance, whose members include Microsoft, Oracle and IBM, said about three-quarters of software installed on personal computers in Vietnam was unlicensed, citing a 2017 survey. It criticised what it described as "inadequate enforcement", despite repeated commitments by Vietnam to address the issue.
The Motion Picture Association said Vietnam was a major hub for online piracy, hosting websites distributing stolen film and television content that attracted over 12.5 billion visits worldwide last year. It called for stronger enforcement and improved market access for legitimate streaming services.

Title: Dollar rangebound ahead of US midterms; bitcoin reels from crypto heist
Article:
SINGAPORE: The dollar and other major currencies were in a holding pattern on Monday as investors turned their attention to this week's US midterm elections, which could shift the balance of power in Congress and control over the federal purse strings.
In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin and ether were nursing losses following last week's record US$6.3 billion heist at Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange.
Traders were bracing for a packed week dominated by the US midterm elections, October US jobs data and central bank rate decisions in the UK, Australia, Norway and Sweden.
Ahead of the week's events, the euro languished near a 17-month low at US$1.1159 in early Asian trade, weighed down by Fitch's revision of France's outlook to "negative" from "stable" after Friday's close.
Sterling was little changed at US$1.3387, while the dollar steadied at 101.94 against a basket of currencies.
Americans head to the polls on Tuesday to determine whether Democrats can wrest control of Congress away from US President ​Donald Trump's Republican Party. Democrats are widely predicted to win the House of Representatives, but the Senate is more in doubt.
"The challenge we face in analysing election outcomes is that polling suggests strong anti-incumbent sentiment, but that does not always translate into actual election outcomes - as we have seen in Brazil and now in Israel," said Eric Robertsen, global head of research and chief strategist at Standard Chartered.
In the event of a Democratic sweep of Congress, Robertsen said capex plans for data centres and AI infrastructure could face increasing obstacles at the state level, while the next debate on raising the US debt ceiling would be among the most contentious in recent history.
Meanwhile, Andreja Cobeljic, head of derivatives trading at AMINA Bank, said hedge funds had suffered "significant losses" in October, leaving markets with "little capacity" to absorb any surprises from the midterm elections.
In other currencies, the yen eased 0.15 per cent to 157.78 per dollar. The Australian dollar was flat at US$0.7033 ahead of Tuesday's policy decision, where the Reserve Bank of Australia is widely expected to raise its cash rate to a near two-decade high of 4.85 per cent.
The New Zealand dollar fell 0.11 per cent to US$0.5625, having slid 1.2 per cent last week in the wake of its central bank's surprise decision to leave rates unchanged.
Elsewhere, bitcoin was up 0.22 per cent at US$77,975.62, having fallen to a six-week low on Friday. Ether was up 0.27 per cent to US$2,268.42, having similarly slid to a two-month trough last week.
Binance customers pulled US$3.64 billion, or 2.1 per cent of its assets, as the exchange went back online on Sunday after hackers the FBI links to North Korea stole billions from the platform last week.
Binance said withdrawals were stabilising after an initial spike and deposit volumes had remained "substantial". The exchange said it had now covered 95 per cent of the US$6.3 billion of stolen assets.
"The crypto industry has spent a decade making blockchains mathematically secure. It still runs on the assumption that an employee's laptop can be trusted," said Richard Forss, chief technology officer at global prime broker EXANTE. "That assumption is now the weakest point in digital finance."

Title: Asia shares bend under AI stress; Apple earnings loom
Article:
SYDNEY: Asian share markets slipped on Monday as worries about the sustainability of the artificial intelligence (AI) investment boom loomed over the tech sector, while the high price of oil limited the safe-haven appeal of sovereign bonds.
Concerns about negative cash flow and the sheer scale of AI capex saw the cost of insuring against corporate defaults blow out last week, while gold hit a one-year low amid talk stressed investors were selling to raise money for margin calls.
An added wrinkle is the midterm elections in the United States, where a win by Democrats in either or both houses could result in more political hurdles for data centres.
Adding to the air of unease were withdrawals from Binance as the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange went back online on Sunday after hackers stole billions from the platform last week.
All of which raises the stakes for earnings this week with Apple, AMD and Palantir set to report in the wake of Intel's near 29 per cent tumble on Friday.
Analysts at Goldman Sachs expect capex by hyperscalers to almost double to US$800 billion this year, and rise further to US$1.2 trillion in 2027. At the same time, they see S&P 500 earnings per share growth of nearly 30 per cent in 2026, slowing to 18 per cent next year.
"Earnings results have underscored the fundamental challenge facing equity investors - earnings growth is strong, but it is no longer accelerating," wrote Ben Snider, Goldman's chief US equity strategist, in a note.
"Similarly, third quarter results support our view that AI investment spending will continue to grow but that the growth rate of AI capex is peaking."
Japan's Nikkei fell 0.5 per cent, while South Korea lost 0.8 per cent, having shed 16 per cent last month. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan eased 0.4 per cent.
In Europe, EUROSTOXX 50 futures firmed 0.1 per cent, while DAX futures were flat.
MORE RATE HIKES COMING
On Wall Street, S&P 500 futures edged up 0.4 per cent, while Nasdaq futures bounced 0.6 per cent. The tech-heavy Nasdaq lost almost 7 per cent in October for its worst month since the Liberation Day tariff rout of April 2025.
The retreat in equities provided a reprieve to safe-haven bonds, with investors wondering if a sustained selloff in the stock market could deter the Federal Reserve from hiking interest rates in December.
Futures still imply a 72 per cent chance of a quarter-point rate rise, but now only have 55 basis points of total tightening priced in compared to more than 70 basis points a month ago.
Yields on 10-year Treasuries nudged up to 4.952 per cent, but remained well off their October peak of 5.3645 per cent, while two-year yields stood at 4.612 per cent.
Among central banks meeting this week, markets are wagering on hikes from the Reserve Bank of Australia, Bank of England and Riksbank, while the Norges Bank is seen on hold.
Economic data due this week includes the influential US ISM survey of manufacturing for October later Monday, while the all-important payrolls report is on Friday.
Median forecasts are for a 65,000 rise in jobs, after September's disappointing 29,000 gain, with the unemployment rate holding at 4.2 per cent.
In currency markets, the majors were pretty much sidelined while all the action was concentrated in stocks. The euro was flat at US$1.1156, while the dollar was barely changed at 157.62 yen.
For commodities, oil prices slipped after Iranian and Qatari officials held a third straight day of talks aimed at pushing for a deal to end the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Brent futures dipped 1.5 per cent to US$111.72 a barrel, though that follows a 13.6 per cent jump in October, while US crude futures eased 1.7 per cent to US$102.37 a barrel.
Non-interest-bearing gold bounced 0.6 per cent to US$3,898 an ounce, having fallen 6.8 per cent last month.

Title: Ringgit opens higher on expectations of OPR normalisation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar and major currencies on Monday, supported by expectations of a possible overnight policy rate (OPR) normalisation ahead of Bank Negara Malaysia's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting this Thursday.
At 8am, the local note was slightly higher at 4.0550/0635 against the greenback from last Friday's close of 4.0555/0600.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid opined that the MPC members would decide to raise the OPR by 25 basis points (bps).
He said the pre-emptive rate cut in July 2025, which lowered the OPR from three per cent to 2.75 per cent, had served its purpose, as concerns over slower economic growth following the tariff shock had not materialised.
"In 2025, the gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 5.2 per cent while in the first nine months of 2026, GDP growth accelerated to 5.5 per cent.
"On that note, the case for OPR normalisation is clear as the fears of slower growth following the tariff shock have not materialised. As such, this could provide support for the ringgit today," he told Bernama.
However, he said market consensus was that the benchmark interest rate would remain unchanged at 2.75 per cent.
On external developments, he said currency markets were expected to remain cautious ahead of the United States midterm elections on Tuesday, particularly amid uncertainties surrounding the conflict in West Asia.
Against major currencies, the ringgit rose against the British pound to 5.4276/4390 from 5.4461/4522 at last Friday's close, gained against the euro to 4.5238/5332 from 4.5413/5464, and strengthened vis-a-vis the Japanese yen to 2.5715/5771 from 2.5782/5812 previously.
The ringgit traded mixed against its Asean peers.
It climbed against the Singapore dollar to 3.1724/1793 from 3.1753/1791 and advanced against the Thai baht to 12.0024/0400 from 12.0373/0561 previously.
The local currency was flat against the Indonesian rupiah at 223.4/224.0 and the Philippine peso at 6.36/6.38, compared with last Friday's close.

Title: Police probe residents' escape from Klang rehabilitation centre
Article:

Title: Bank of England poised to raise rates but may push back on bets for more
Article:
MANCHESTER: The Bank of England (BoE) is expected to bow to inflation pressure from soaring energy costs and raise interest rates on Thursday, though it may push back against investors' bets that several more increases will follow next year.
Economists polled by Reuters expect the BoE to raise Bank Rate to four per cent from 3.75 per cent, its first hike since August 2023, when inflation was still more than triple its two per cent target.
The BoE was criticised for underestimating how persistent inflation would prove the last time energy costs surged, and it is wary of being caught out again, with global energy prices high and little sign of a lasting end to the Iran war.
Back then, the BoE was among the first major central banks to raise rates. This time the US Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank have moved first.
BANK OF ENGLAND'S HAND "INCREASINGLY FORCED"
Governor Andrew Bailey has said the BoE cannot wait for conclusive proof of second-round effects, where higher inflation feeds into wage- and price-setting, or it will act too late.
But how much evidence is enough, and whether the drawn-out Iran war makes some second-round effects inevitable, have divided the Monetary Policy Committee, which voted 6-3 to hold rates in September.
Bailey said last month that businesses he had spoken to seemed to be absorbing higher costs more than in 2022.
In September the BoE warned that inflation would rise above four per cent early next year, and said the jump in energy prices since its July forecasts bore similarities to its "adverse" scenario, in which inflation risked becoming entrenched.
Inflation has since run hotter than the BoE expected. Consumer prices rose 3.5 per cent in the year to September, compared with the central bank's July forecast of three per cent.
"In other words, their hands are increasingly being forced, whether they like it or not," said Stefan Koopman, senior macro strategist at Rabobank.
"At some point, even a committee that would probably rather sit tight has to make good on at least some of what is priced (in the market). That time is now."
SOME MPC MEMBERS HAVE CRITICISED THE BOE
The Reuters poll pointed to a 7-2 vote in favour of a hike, with external members Alan Taylor and Swati Dhingra seen as most likely to continue to vote to keep rates steady.
Both have stressed spare capacity in the economy as a reason to wait, though recent growth figures have surprised to the upside.
Hawkish policymakers such as chief economist Huw Pill and external members Catherine Mann and Megan Greene have criticised the BoE's handling of the current episode.
But even they may baulk at endorsing market pricing of three to four more quarter-point hikes in 2027, which would take Bank Rate to between 4.75 per cent and five per cent.
"While we don't expect a clear steer from the Committee on how many hikes they're planning, it's possible that the meeting minutes or Bailey ... signal that Bank Rate is unlikely to reach the level that is priced in by financial markets," said Alexander Harvey, UK economist at consultancy Oxford Economics.
STATEMENTS WILL OFFER CLUES TO RATES OUTLOOK
Harvey said individual MPC members' statements would offer important clues to the outlook, particularly those of the BoE's internal members, whose views have been finely balanced.
Unlike financial markets, economists polled by Reuters last month were split on whether further hikes would follow after November's.
Mann has argued that aggressive bets on rate hikes reflect a risk premium the BoE itself exacerbated by adopting a "wait-and-see" stance after war broke out in the Middle East, rather than signalling clearly that it would keep inflation in check.
Alongside new economic forecasts, investors will be watching for the BoE's initial assessment of finance minister John Healey's budget, delivered last week.
Healey offered modest support to households and motorists struggling with higher energy costs, funded partly by a tax on banks. Economists said the measures would only slightly reduce the expected rise in inflation.
The BoE announces its decision at 1200 GMT on Thursday, with Bailey and some of his deputies holding a press conference at 1230 GMT.

Title: Official: Four US citizens, Canadian among Spain train crash dead
Article:
MADRID, (Spain): Four US citizens and one each from Canada, Japan, Argentina, Mexico, Tunisia and the Czech Republic were among the 69 killed in last week's high-speed train collision in Spain, authorities said.
Wednesday's disaster — one of Europe's deadliest rail accidents this century — has seen victims' relatives endure an agonising wait as forensics teams identify the dead, sometimes from individual body parts.
A legal body set up to handle the identification work, made up of police and forensics experts, announced in a statement late on Sunday the 10 latest confirmed foreign victims.
It had already announced the deaths of a French and a Portuguese citizen, as well as that of 54 Spaniards.
All but three of the victims are now identified, the statement added.
Three reports for missing people remain active, the authorities said. They concern two Australians and one Japanese citizen.
"As the contacted families have expressed their wish to travel to Spain to carry out in-person identification, we are awaiting their arrival in the country," the statement said.
The accident was Spain's second high-speed train collision this year and raised fresh questions about the country's rail safety, after a crash in the southern region of Andalusia in January killed 46 people.
The latest disaster struck when a service by state operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to Spanish company Iryo outside the central village of Urda, around 130 kilometres (80 miles) south of Madrid.
The failure of an automatic safety system halted all trains on a 63-kilometre stretch of track, but a control centre authorised the Renfe service to resume its journey while the other train was still.
The tragedy came one month before a November 29 general election in which Socialist leader Pedro Sanchez will seek to overcome unfavourable polls and extend his eight-year premiership. — AFP

Title: Oil slips more than 1pct as talks continue on ending Iran war
Article:
SINGAPORE: Oil prices slipped more than one per cent on Monday after Iranian and Qatari officials held a third straight day of talks aimed at pushing for a deal to end the US-Israeli war on Iran.
Brent crude futures fell US$1.59, or 1.40 per cent, to US$111.84 a barrel by 0011 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$102.56 a barrel, down US$1.56, or 1.50 per cent.
Brent ended October at its highest level in six months amid concerns that the US-Iran conflict could escalate again after Tuesday's US midterm elections.
"Oil is seeing a technical pullback this morning after last week's strong gains," said Tim Waterer, chief ⁠market analyst at KCM Trade.
"Lingering hopes of some form of diplomatic progress, combined with the absence of any meaningful military escalation over the weekend, have taken some of the immediate heat out of prices for now."
However, the market remained alert to the possibility that rhetoric around Iran could be ratcheted higher and push Brent toward US$120 after the midterm elections, Waterer said.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Sunday that the purpose of the "ongoing and progressing" talks was to continue consultations with the Qatari mediators, adding Tehran is prepared for "both defence and diplomacy".
The talks come amid attacks on oil tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz that are driving up global energy and shipping costs. In October, Saudi Arabia increased crude exports versus September despite attacks by the Iran-aligned Yemeni Houthis on its energy infrastructure, two of three ship-tracking companies said.
The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries and allies including Russia, or OPEC+, kept December production targets steady on Sunday, confirming expectations that more policy adjustments will not occur until next year, as the group continues to struggle with export disruptions from the Iran war.

Title: Sarawak's economic paradox
Article:
SARAWAK presents Malaysia with a revealing economic question. How can a state rank among the country's strongest producers of economic value while its typical household receives less income than the national median?
The Statistics Department revised 2024 figures bring the question into focus. Sarawak logged gross domestic product (GDP) per capita of RM73,253, above the national figure of RM56,772.
Yet its median gross monthly household income was RM5,504, compared with Malaysia's RM7,017. Its mean household income, RM6,947, was also below the national average of RM9,155.
Using 2024 provides a common reference year for production and household income. The figures describe different aspects of prosperity.
Their divergence deserves a careful explanation and should inform how development is assessed.
TWO MEASURES OF PROSPERITY
GDP measures the value added by production within a territory. GDP per capita divides that annual value by the population.
It is neither an average salary nor the amount available for each resident to spend.
Household income records receipts from employment, self-employment, property and investment, and transfers.
The median identifies the household in the middle of the income distribution. The department's household survey covers Malaysian citizen households, while GDP has a broader production coverage.
These measures therefore have different units and coverage.
Subtracting monthly household income from annual GDP per capita would produce no meaningful estimate of wealth lost or income retained.
The useful comparison concerns their positions against the corresponding national benchmarks.
Sarawak's oil and gas, liquefied natural gas and energy-intensive industries help explain its substantial production base.
Such activities require considerable capital and can generate high value with relatively few workers. Their productivity need not be reflected in the earnings of people employed elsewhere in the economy.
Ownership matters. Income generated within a state can accrue to companies, investors or workers resident elsewhere.
Corporate earnings may be retained for investment or distributed to shareholders. Tax revenues may finance services across the federation.
The geography of production consequently differs from the geography of income received. The size of these flows must be established through evidence.
The headline figures alone cannot tell us which mechanism contributes most to Sarawak's household income position.
FOLLOW THE INCOME
A more useful inquiry begins with the industries. How much income do they generate for resident workers? What business do they create for local firms? How do those firms improve productivity and pay?
Consider two industrial projects of comparable size. One might procure most specialist services externally and offer limited opportunities for local suppliers.
Another might develop engineering companies, train technicians and establish sustained ties relationships with nearby firmsenterprises.
Their investment announcements could look similar, while their wider economic consequences differ substantially.
This is an illustration of what should be investigated. Establishing the pattern in Sarawak requires procurement, employment and ownership evidence.
A supplier's registered address alone would reveal little about where its work is performed or how much value it adds locally.
The accounting must be precise. Imported intermediate inputs are excluded when domestic value added is calculated. They should not then be deducted from GDP a second time.
Imported machinery and expertise can improve productivity and create opportunities. Purchases from other states can support a more competitive Sarawak industry.
Successful integration should boost increase Sarawak's ability to earn income through national and international supply chains.
Keeping every ringgit within state boundaries would be an unsuitable objective.
Households benefit through public services. Resource-related revenues can support education, healthcare and infrastructure even when those benefits do not appear as cash income in a household survey.
Any assessment of prosperity must consider this wider contribution, alongside the costs families face and the quality of services they receive.
MEASURE WHAT FAMILIES GAIN
The policy implication is to examine the connection between productive industries and the people living around them.
More investment can expand opportunities, but its contribution to household prosperity depends on the jobs, supplier ties and public benefits it creates.
Regional input-output accounts could help map purchases between industries and across state boundaries.
Linking these accounts to labour-market, ownership and household data through a regional social accounting matrix would provide a fuller picture of how income reaches different groups.
An ordinary input-output table cannot identify every household beneficiary or the ultimate recipients of company dividends.
A useful assessment would track resident earnings, access to skilled work and the value added by local suppliers.
It should distinguish developments in industrial centres from conditions in more remote communities. State averages can conceal differences that require different policy responses.
Public reporting should distinguish projected benefits from realised outcomes.
Investment approvals and modelled multipliers provide useful information, but families experience actual wages, dependable services and opportunities that they can reach. Those outcomes deserve equal prominence in the development account.
This would make the debate more constructive. It would help governments identify where infrastructure is still the binding constraint, where skills are scarce and where firms need support to meet industrial requirements. It would also allow successful programmes to be recognised on evidence.
Sarawak's productive strength gives it substantial opportunities. The next task is to show how effectively that strength improves the economic lives of its people.
A state's prosperity acquires its fullest meaning when households can see the gains in their earnings, security and opportunities.
*Economist Samirul Ariff Othman is an international relations analyst and a senior consultant with Global Asia Consulting (GAC). Samirul has a background as a senior researcher at the Malaysian Institute of Economic Research. The viewpoints articulated are solely those of the author.
