Title: The case of Maxis – U Mobile merger
Article:
The rumour mill is back spinning with the story of a merger between Maxis Bhd and U Mobile Sdn Bhd.
While the recent report by a foreign wire service on the possibility of a merger between Maxis and U Mobile is not the first time such a story had come up, it still attracts market attention due to the impact it could have on the country's telecom sector.
A merged Maxis-U Mobile entity would overtake CelcomDigi Bhd as the country's largest mobile operator by subscribers. As of Oct 30, Maxis is valued at RM27.9 billion, while CelcomDigi is about RM1 billion bigger in market value.
After the story broke last Wednesday (Oct 28), Maxis' shareholders reacted negatively to the story, with its share price falling 3.8 per cent to close at RM3.51. The stock fell 5.2 per cent during trading hours that day, the biggest intraday decline since June.
The negative reaction to the story could be due to the dilutive impact that such a merger would have on Maxis' shares, depending on the valuation of U Mobile agreed by both companies. The higher the valuation, the more dilution to Maxis' share value.
What is the value of U Mobile for Maxis, if indeed the companies are courting each other?
In a statement to Business Times' queries, Maxis said it is always evaluating strategic opportunities and partnerships that are value accretive. A merger with U Mobile can be value accretive to Maxis, in the long run, due to the second 5G network.
U Mobile operates Malaysia's second 5G network alongside Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB). The asset that U Mobile has – 100MHz block within the 3.5Ghz and 3.6GHz band – is what makes it valuable.
Malaysia's 5G network operates on a dual network model. DNB, which was supposed to be the country's sole operator until the change in policy in 2024, operates the network on two 100MHz blocks between the 3.3GHz and 3.4GHz, and 3.4GHz and 3.5GHz bands.
Currently, Maxis, CelcomDigi and YTL Communications Sdn Bhd are on DNB's network. The three are also equal shareholders of DNB, after the Minister of Finance Inc (MoF Inc) exercised its put option requiring them to acquire its shares on Dec 1, 2025.
U Mobile had exited DNB on June 30, following its appointment as the second 5G network operator.
However, developing the 5G network is not cheap. According to a telco executive, one 5G site costs around RM200,000 to be developed, excluding equipment. DNB had set up 7,489 sites in developing the network.
"The cost of investment in the 5G network might not be justified, if not shared across operators, as average revenue per users (ARPU) has been declining over the past few years," says the telco executive Business Times spoke to.
In the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, Maxis' postpaid ARPU declined 1.1 per cent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) to RM70.50 per month, while CelcomDigi's fell 4.5 per cent QoQ to RM60.
"Customers are not willing to pay more for data. If a mobile network operator (MNO) wants to invest in a network, it will need to grow its customer base tremendously, which is perhaps the reason for the Maxis-U Mobile merger to come up again," the executive says.
When DNB was rolled out as the country's sole 5G network operator, the cost was touted at RM16.5 billion over 10 years. Recently, DNB raised a RM5.2 billion Islamic syndicated financing to refinance its government guarantee revolving credit, as well as for further investments.
A look at U Mobile's financials with the Companies Commission of Malaysia reveals that the company has an accumulated loss of RM6.3 billion as of Dec 31, 2025, with a net loss of RM1.6 billion during the year.
This shows that while U Mobile has been growing its subscribers, it has yet to translate into profitability.
MERGER MUST GET CELCOMDIGI, YTL POWER'S AGREEMENTS
A merger between Maxis and U Mobile also depends on whether Maxis could get out of DNB. This is because a telco is not allowed to have ownerships in both 5G networks.
Currently, Maxis, CelcomDigi and YTL Power International Bhd each own 33.33 per cent of DNB. If Maxis were to merge with U Mobile, it would have to sell its stake to either CelcomDigi or YTL Power, or both.
Considering that each company already holding 33.33 per cent stake, a sale of Maxis' stake would mean DNB will be a subsidiary of both CelcomDigi and YTL Power. Whether this is something palatable for either is a question.
As of the financial year ended Dec 31, 2024, DNB recorded a net loss of RM1.2 billion, and accumulated loss of RM3.16 billion. The network operator is expected to remain loss-making until 2030.
Throughout the years, the shareholding structure of DNB has been changed twice. The first happened in June 2024, when CelcomDigi, Maxis, U Mobile and YTL Power collectively acquired 65.1 per cent stake, giving each an interest of approximately 16.3 per cent.
When U Mobile became the second network operator, it disposed of its 100,000 DNB shares to CelcomDigi, Maxis and YTL, giving the remaining shareholders 19.44 per cent each. Then their shareholdings increased to 33.33 per cent following the put option exercised by MoF Inc.
The put option requires each of the remaining shareholders to fork out RM327.87 million to MoF Inc.
While the exercise is not yet completed, the exit of the government-owned company also means that the private investors now have to hold the risks of developing the 5G network themselves.
The transfer of ownership is expected to be completed by the end of this year. This means that DNB associate contributions will begin appearing in Maxis, CelcomDigi, and YTL Power's financial statements from the fourth quarter of 2026.
The full impact of DNB's contributions to profit and loss will be felt in 2027.
Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) in a research note on Oct 29 stated that it had flagged a Maxis – U Mobile merger as a live risk weighing on both Maxis and CelcomDigi.
"If the merger materialises, we believe the near-term implications would be negative given higher capex for 5G, weaker earnings, and dividend pressures for both Maxis and CelcomDigi.
"But, beyond that, the prospect of a market repair in a two-player market is strong because the aggressive price competitor (i.e. U Mobile) is being absorbed, which should reinforce pricing discipline in the market," said HLIB.
A merger between Maxis and U Mobile would create a more meaningful two-player market, as the combined entity would have a subscriber base that is broadly on par with CelcomDigi. On top of that, Telekom Malaysia Bhd is also on the second network.
But it will also put pressure on CelcomDigi and YTL Power to shoulder the cost of developing DNB's network. Will they then, if the merger were to happen, acquire Maxis' shares in DNB?

Title: Simpan SSPN 'one of the best' for  savings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:   Malaysians have deposited RM26.07 billion in savings into the National Higher Education Fund Corporation's (PTPTN) Simpan SSPN, with 7.74 million accounts recorded up to  Sept 30, says  its   chairman Datuk Seri Norliza Abdul Rahim.
She said the figures underscored Simpan SSPN's continued relevance as a savings scheme for higher education in Malaysia.
"This performance proves that Simpan SSPN remains strong and relevant as one of the best education saving schemes in Malaysia," she said at the closing ceremony of BMS 2026 and World Savings Day celebration on Saturday.
Simpan SSPN encourages Malaysians to save early for their children's higher education, helping to reduce the reliance on education loans.
Norliza said deposits collected during the Simpan SSPN Savings Month (BMS) 2026 campaign, from Sept 25 to Oct 29, amounted to RM267.7 million, which exceeded the RM250 million target by 7.1 per cent.
"PTPTN is optimistic that deposit collections in conjunction with BMS 2026 will continue to increase and record even more encouraging results.
"Behind this achievement, more parents have taken early steps to prepare education savings for their children. Congratulations and well done to all PTPTN personnel for their efforts," she said.
Meanwhile, visitor Lim Eu Jack said Simpan SSPN offered a practical way to save for education while enjoying tax relief of up to RM8,000 annually.
"With this SSPN savings, besides allowing me to put money in one place, at the same time, I can also get a tax rebate of up to RM8,000, and that's quite a lot.
"So, this extra money can help support our  expenses," he said.
Besides tax relief, Simpan SSPN also offers takaful protection, free matching grants of up to RM10,000 for eligible families, competitive dividend rates, syariah-compliant savings and a government guarantee.
Its prize draw campaign, held with BMS 2026, offered prizes worth nearly RM1.9 million to 1,060 winners. Launched in 2018, BMS is in its ninth year and serves  as a platform to raise awareness about early financial planning for education and the benefits of saving in Simpan SSPN.
The World Savings Day on Oct 31, with  the theme "AI advises, Human decides", highlighted technology's role in financial planning while emphasising the importance of personal discipline and commitment to saving.

Title: Health Ministry faces shortage of 1,176 drivers, including ambulance personnel
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — The Health Ministry (MoH) is reportedly facing a nationwide shortage of 1,176 vehicle drivers, including those assigned to ambulances, with the vacancies expected to persist until at least April next year.
Berita Harian
reported that the ministry attributed the shortage to delays in recruiting General Service Assistants (Driving) after the Public Service Department temporarily suspended recruitment through the Public Services Commission (PSC) in 2024 to facilitate implementation of the new Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA).
Under the SSPA, the former vehicle driver scheme was merged into the new General Service Assistant scheme, requiring recruitment requirements to be reviewed, particularly for personnel tasked with driving ambulances.
According to the report, MoH said it expects the vacant driving posts at public health facilities to be filled in stages from April 2027, subject to the completion of the PSC recruitment process.
As of September 30, the ministry had 8,863 General Service Assistant (Driving) positions, of which 7,687 were filled, according to figures provided by MoH to Berita Harian.
Peninsular Malaysia accounted for 1,003 of the vacancies, followed by Sarawak with 92, Sabah with 73 and Labuan with eight.
The ministry reportedly said recruitment projections would also have to account for existing vacancies, retirements, staff attrition and the operational requirements of individual facilities.
It added that applications were still being processed by the PSC, while the driving competency test for candidates was completed on October 27.
The shortage comes as the government plans to procure 400 new ambulances for MoH hospitals under Budget 2027, a measure intended to improve emergency response times.
Berita Harian
had earlier reported concerns from PEMATA-KKM president Reostam Dzahar that the shortage was increasing the workload of existing drivers, with some allegedly working beyond stipulated hours and experiencing burnout.

Title: Takiyuddin: Perikatan not part of Bersatu MPs’ CSA, won’t sign deal just for allocations
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 2 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) was not involved in negotiations for the confidence-and-supply agreement (CSA) signed by six Bersatu MPs with the federal government and will not enter such a deal merely to secure constituency allocations, its secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan reportedly said.
Utusan Malaysia
reported today that Takiyuddin said the agreement was a decision by the lawmakers involved and did not represent PN’s official position as an opposition bloc.
“The CSA was their own choice as MPs. Coincidentally, those who joined the CSA are from groups that are not actively involved in PN, namely Bersatu itself, former Bersatu members who previously switched parties, and Muda,” he was quoted as saying.
“So, PN was not involved in the negotiations or the signing. We were not involved,” he reportedly added.
Six Bersatu MPs led by party president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin signed the CSA on October 29 alongside Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and six former Bersatu MPs who now sit as independents.
Under the agreement, the participating Bersatu MPs agreed to support Budget 2027, while the government agreed to provide them with constituency development allocations equal to those received by government MPs.
The agreement also covers proposed institutional reforms, including limiting the prime minister’s tenure to two terms and separating the roles of the Attorney-General and Public Prosecutor.
Takiyuddin also told
Utusan Malaysia
that Bersatu’s decision to use its own logo in the November 14 Melaka state election had neither been formally communicated to PN nor received the coalition’s approval.
He said PN’s constitution allows component parties to contest under their own logos with the coalition’s consent, adding that PN was examining possible disciplinary matters involving Bersatu.
Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali had earlier confirmed that the party would use its own logo in the state election, saying the decision had been approved by Muhyiddin and communicated to the Election Commission.
Separately, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said welcomed proposals to expand the CSA to other opposition parties, saying broader cross-party cooperation could help build parliamentary consensus for institutional reforms.
PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, meanwhile, responded to criticism of the CSA from PAS by pointing out that Malaysia’s previous cross-party agreement was signed in 2021 when PAS was part of the federal Cabinet.

Title: DAP confirms seven seats for Sarawak polls, mulls Batu Lintang as eighth
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 2 — DAP will contest seven seats in Kuching and Bau areas in the upcoming 13th Sarawak State Election, said its state chairman Chong Chieng Jen.
According to Chong, who chaired the party’s state committee meeting earlier yesterday, the seven confirmed seats are Padungan, Pending, Batu Kitang, Kota Sentosa, Batu Kawah, Tasik Biru and Opar.
“We are also considering Batu Lintang as a possible eighth seat.
“Our focus remains on bringing more voices into the State Legislative Assembly and ensuring stronger checks and balances for the people of Sarawak,” he posted on Facebook yesterday.
Chong said the party would announce its decisions on the seats in Sibu, Sarikei, Bintulu and Miri within the next one to two weeks.
In the 12th Sarawak State Election held in 2021, DAP only won two out of 26 seats it contested, namely Padungan dan Pending.
Ruling coalition Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) swept 76 of the 82 seats contested, while Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) won four seats.
The Election Commission (EC) will hold a special meeting on November 6 to discuss key dates for the 13th Sarawak state election. — Bernama

Title: ‘Do not be discouraged’: Anwar backs Hakim Danish after fourth-place Moto3 finish
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has offered words of encouragement to young Malaysian rider Muhammad Hakim Danish Ramli after he finished fourth in the Moto3 race at the Malaysian Motorcycle Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit yesterday.
While congratulating him, the Prime Minister hoped the 19-year-old rider would continue to strive in the remaining races of the season.
“Congratulations to Hakim Danish for finishing fourth in the Moto3 race! Keep working hard and do not be discouraged. There are still races remaining, so keep pushing to go further,” he said in a post on X.
Anwar said that besides Hakim Danish, he also took time to meet young Malaysian riders Muhammad Qabil Irfan Azlan, Qayyim Razin Razali and Muhammad Naqib Rifqi Zulhelmi.
“I also reminded them not to give up easily when faced with challenges because every champion has also gone through ups and downs.
“I hope that one day you too will become an inspiration to more Malaysian youngsters to make the country proud on the world stage,” he said.
Hakim Danish, who rides for the AEON Credit-MT Helmets-MSi team, missed out on a podium finish on home soil after completing the race in fourth place, just 4.410 seconds behind Spanish winner Maximo Quiles.
The Terengganu-born rider put in a competitive performance, moving up to second place on the 11th lap before being overtaken by two challengers on the following lap.
Hakim Danish had also secured podium finishes at the Italian GP and Czech Republic GP this season, demonstrating his ability to compete with the world’s best riders in the Moto3 category.
According to the MotoGP calendar, the season now has three rounds remaining, in Qatar, Portugal and Spain. — Bernama

Title: KL police investigate after woman allegedly assaults two children at shopping mall
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Police are investigating the incident involving an unknown woman who shoved and hit two children at a shopping mall here yesterday.
Dang Wangi district police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said they found a 35-second video that went viral on social media depicting an argument between two individuals following the incident, adding that the father of a child involved in the incident, aged 36, lodged a police report at 7.39pm.
“The complainant said that an unknown woman had suddenly shoved his son from behind, causing him to fall, while he was walking with his two children, aged two and seven at about 3pm.
“The woman also allegedly hit the back of his two year old daughter,” he said in a statement last night, adding that the police viewed the incident seriously and a comprehensive investigation is ongoing to identify the real cause of the incident.
He also advised the public to refrain from speculating and urged those with information to contact the Kuala Lumpur police hotline at 03-2115 9999, the Dang Wangi district police headquarters at 03-2600 2222 or the nearest police station. — Bernama

Title: Teenage girl falls from second floor of Tampoi flat after suffering seizure
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 2 — A teenage girl sustained injuries after having a seizure while peering over a staircase wall, before falling from the second floor of a flat in the Tampoi area here yesterday.
Acting Johor Bahru Utara district police chief Supt Azrol Anuar Nor said his team received a report at about 12.20pm regarding the incident involving the 18-year-old victim.
He said the victim was found lying conscious on the sidewalk beside the flat building. Preliminary investigation results indicate that the victim was believed to have suffered a seizure while peering down over the staircase wall, before falling from the second floor of the flat.
“The victim suffered injuries to the back of the head as well as to the neck, left wrist and right leg, and is currently receiving treatment at Sultanah Aminah Hospital here,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Azrol Anuar also said that the police have identified four witnesses and will record their statements to complete the investigation.
“The public is advised not to make any speculation that could interfere with the investigation, and any information related to the incident should be channelled to 07-5563122,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Inmates taken from Klang rehab centre: Police open criminal trespass probe
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 2 — Police are investigating a trespassing case involving a group suspected of removing several inmates from a private rehabilitation centre in Bukit Kuda, near here, without the management's permission.
Klang Utara police chief ACP Ramsay Embol said police received a report from the rehabilitation centre’s owner on October 28 that a group of unknown men and women had entered the premises and taken several inmates away.
“Police confirm the incident and the case is being investigated under Section 447 of the Penal Code for criminal trespass,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Following the incident, Ramsay advised the public not to speculate on the case because it could threaten public order and disrupt police investigations.
Those with information regarding the incident are urged to contact the Klang Utara District Police Headquarters at 03-32919614 or the investigating officer, Sgt Amirul Ashraf Abd Rahim, at 011-69730086.
Earlier, a 38-second video was circulated on social media showing several individuals, believed to be inmates, leaving a rehabilitation centre in Klang. — Bernama

Title: Man smashes five bank machines after failed ATM withdrawal in Sarikei, injures one person
Article:
SARIKEI, Nov 2 — Angered after failing to withdraw cash from an automated teller machine (ATM), a man vandalised five banking machines using a machete before allegedly injuring a young man who tried to stop him in an incident on Jalan Masjid Lama, near here, early yesterday morning.
Sarikei district police chief Supt Aswandy Anis said the 38-year-old suspect is believed to have damaged two ATM machines, two cash deposit machines (CDM), and one cheque deposit machine at a bank around 12.05am.
He said the initial investigation found that the suspect acted this way due to dissatisfaction after failing to withdraw money from the ATM, and also admitted to being intoxicated at the time of the incident.
“After the incident, the suspect is believed to have fled by driving a Toyota Hilux against the flow of traffic before crashing into a road divider on Jalan Masjid Lama,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Aswandy said that at a nearby location, a 21-year-old man sustained severe injuries to his left hand after allegedly being struck with a machete by the suspect while attempting to stop him.
He said the victim was then taken to Sarikei Hospital for further treatment.
“The suspect then surrendered at the Sarikei police station and the police also seized a Toyota Hilux and a machete believed to have been used in the incident,” he said.
According to him, the urine screening test found the suspect positive for the drugs, ketamine and benzodiazepine, while a check revealed that the man had no previous criminal record.
The case is being investigated under Section 427 and Section 326 of the Penal Code, Section 45(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, and Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia’s first FA-50M jets arrive at Kuantan base for final acceptance tests
Article:
KUANTAN, Nov 2 — Two FA-50M aircraft arrived at the airbase here yesterday, marking the first delivery of the 18 aircraft to be acquired by the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) from Korea Aerospace Industries.
According to a post on the RMAF’s Facebook page, the aircraft departed Labuan Air Base at 1.45pm and landed at the Kuantan Airbase at 3.38pm, witnessed by Chief of Air Force General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris.
Both aircraft departed from Sacheon, South Korea, on October 29 before making several transit stops in Jeju, Laoag in the Philippines, and Labuan.
The FA-50M aircraft M58-01 was piloted by KAI pilot Lee Donkyu, together with No. 15 Squadron Commanding Officer Major Mohd Jamil Awang, while aircraft M58-02 was piloted by Kim Inchul, together with No. 15 Squadron Executive Officer Major Muhammad Ashraf Wahab.
“Both aircraft will subsequently undergo the Final Acceptance Test process by the RMAF before their official acceptance, which is expected to take place at the end of November 2026,” the post said.
Also present to witness the historic occasion were Deputy Chief of Air Force Lieutenant General Datuk Seri Nur Hafis Abdul Karim, Air Education and Training Commander Lieutenant General Datuk Mohd Sani Omar, and Air Support Commander Major General Datuk Ahmad Khusairi Ahmad Fadli.
Previously, it was reported that the aircraft would be operated by No. 15 Squadron, which currently has more than 200 personnel, with preparations for its operational deployment focused at the RMAF Kuantan Air Base. — Bernama

Title: ‘See you again at Sepang’: Anwar hails Malaysian MotoGP and thanks fans, organisers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated and thanked all staff, organisers, and motorsports fans for successfully hosting the 2026 Malaysian Motorcycle Grand Prix (GP), which ended yesterday at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC).
In a post on his official Facebook page, Anwar described this year's edition as thrilling and vibrant, featuring fierce competition among the world's top riders and memorable moments throughout the event.
“Congratulations to all winners and participating riders. Thank you also to all personnel, organisers, volunteers, and fans for their effort and support in making it successful.
“May the excitement and spirit of motorsports such as MotoGP continue to inspire more young people to fly the Malaysian flag high! See you again at Sepang,” he said.
The Prime Minister also said he met with MotoGP Sports Entertainment Group chief executive officer Carmelo Ezpeleta to exchange views on the sport's development and its potential to raise Malaysia’s international standing.
“We also walked around the track, greeting several riders and personnel who worked tirelessly to ensure this edition of MotoGP ran smoothly and vibrantly,” he said.
Anwar said that beyond the racing action at Sepang, the event should be leveraged for broader economic spillovers, including boosting tourism, creating business opportunities, and driving the local economy.
“This ultimately brings Malaysia closer to motorsports fans around the globe,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Why Malaysia should have national long-term care insurance and how it can be funded
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 2 — If Malaysia introduces a new nationwide insurance to cover the cost of long-term care of older persons, who would be paying for it?
The government via tax revenue? All Malaysians through a monthly contribution? Or a mix of both? Or some other method?
But wait, just what is long-term care insurance?
Unlike a medical card or medical insurance which covers hospital bills, long-term care insurance covers the care and support that a person — including older persons — needs outside of hospitals.
For example, if a person is unable to feed or dress himself/herself due to a stroke or other illnesses.
Social Security Organisation (Socso) Deputy CEO (Strategy and Corporate), Edmund Cheong Peck Huang said Socso or Perkeso already covers long-term care for Malaysian workers by giving them a lifelong monthly “invalidity pension” — but only if they become invalid before age 60.
“The irony of Perkeso being able to provide pension, being able to provide rehabilitation, medical benefits until the person dies is that you have to be sick or injured before 60. Then you would have proper long-term care protection.
“But the thing is that when we talk about long-term care, invalidity or sickness comes after 60. When it comes after 60, who protects you?” the social protection expert said recently at the National Long-Term Care Financing Dialogue 2026.
Cheong said this has led to a “moral hazard” where Malaysians lie and try to claim for this Socso monthly payout before they turn 60, even when they are actually not invalid.
“And to be honest, we are seeing trends of people applying for Perkeso’s invalidity pension at the ages of 55 to 60.
“Basically not because they are invalid, but basically they are trying their luck. Hoping for that lottery that Perkeso says that you are invalid and you get pension for life, you get rehabilitation for life,” he said, adding that the spouse and children would also continue to get a pension as this person’s dependants.
“People are lying so that they get protection. So, we need to have a much more sustainable model for it.”
Edmund Cheong said mandatory contributions by all Malaysians would make long-term care insurance much cheaper, highlighting that everyone grows old and may need long-term care in the future. — Picture by Choo Choy May
‘Solidarity’: Paying for another Malaysian’s care now; getting paid when you become old in the future too
To introduce long-term care insurance for all Malaysians, Cheong proposed making it mandatory for every Malaysian to contribute to it.
“My one answer to it is one word — solidarity. Are we ready for solidarity? Because when we talk about long-term care insurance, it is a social insurance programme. When it is a social insurance programme, it is a mandatory contribution,” he said.
He pointed out that the monthly premium would be very affordable if it is a mandatory scheme involving all Malaysians, compared to a voluntary insurance scheme where the monthly premium would be very high as there would only be a small pool of contributors.
He cautioned Malaysians against being “individualistic” by viewing the contributions as “my savings”, noting that even the most prudent person would not be able to save enough for long-term care in their old age.
Cheong pointed out that everyone grows old, and that paying into this national insurance would eventually end up benefitting us when we need long-term care in the future.
“So that’s where you have to educate, today I’m paying for someone else’s grandfather, but one day, that some random Malaysian will be paying for me,” he said.
He added that a long-lasting organisation with a proper track record and proper infrastructure should be given the trust to run this national insurance scheme, as a person who has contributed for decades to the insurance can then hope to rely on it one day.
Cheong also indicated that long-term care insurance could be funded through existing social protection contributions, pointing out that the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) currently already allows EPF withdrawals via i-Lindung to buy life and critical illness insurance.
“But why can’t we just be brave enough and say, ‘Hey, let’s restructure it’,” he said, noting that social protection organisations such as Socso’s counterparts have also evolved over time to also cover employment injury and invalidity in line with changing needs and social risks.
One example that Cheong cited was Singapore’s national long-term care insurance CareShield Life, which is managed under the country’s Central Provident Fund (CPF) — the equivalent of Malaysia’s EPF.
Syarikat Takaful Malaysia Keluarga Berhad’s Group CEO Nor Azman Zainal said there is a lack of willingness among Malaysians to pay for retirement-related insurance products if it is voluntary. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Why long-term care insurance may fail in Malaysia if it’s not mandatory
Syarikat Takaful Malaysia Keluarga Berhad’s Group CEO Nor Azman Zainal, who has 30 years’ experience in the insurance and takaful sector, indicated that the real challenge was convincing Malaysians that they need retirement-related insurance products.
“From an insurance perspective, I can tell you, based on my observation and our own experience, long-term care is least on the minds of our customers,” he said at the same panel.
Nor Azman pointed to the insurance and takaful sector’s unsuccessful attempts in Malaysia to introduce insurance for Malaysians in their old age, which he said shows it would be tough to introduce new products.
This included life annuity products in the late 1990s and early 2000s that were designed to be funded through EPF, and another new retirement product about 10 to 15 years ago which also failed.
He said the problem with a voluntary long-term care insurance would be “nobody wants to pay for it”, and that it would only work in Malaysia if it is a mandatory nationwide scheme with the government’s involvement similar to that in Singapore or Japan.
“So I think that’s the way forward, but if you leave it entirely to the insurance sector or the takaful sector, we are going to fail once again,” he said.
He said another challenge in Malaysia is the lack of relevant data, which is required by actuaries for cost predictions when designing a long-term care insurance product.
“So I think, in short, it’s going to be tough, but it’s doable,” he said.
ProtectHealth Corporation’s Head of Healthcare (Sustainability and Assurance) Dr Muhammed Anis Abd Wahab said government funding for healthcare and long-term care needs to be increased. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Government needs to fund long-term care in Malaysia too, advocates say
At the same panel, ProtectHealth Corporation’s Head of Healthcare (Sustainability and Assurance) Dr Muhammed Anis Abd Wahab agreed that there needs to be solidarity or shared risk in a single pool for long-term care.
While healthcare and long-term care should be a shared responsibility that also involves Malaysians, Dr Anis said the government has to “predominantly fund most” of those costs and advocated for an increase in government funding for these.
Fellow panellist and Malaysia Caregivers Association (Kendana) chairman Rashidi Yahaya stopped short of advocating for Socso to step up and handle a national long-term care scheme, but said it was capable of doing so.
Rashidi proposed a four-tier approach to financing long-term care in Malaysia, starting with prevention; having a social protection element that is tax-funded; a mandatory contributory fund with contributions from both employers and employees; and then a voluntary private top-up through insurance.
He indicated that Malaysians’ EPF funds could be tapped for long-term care: “We don’t have to go and tell the government tomorrow, ‘let’s start a new legislation, let’s start a new tax fund’, because the money is already there.”
In Singapore, Singaporeans must pay the premiums (typically using their CPF savings) for their mandatory long-term care insurance CareShield Life, but the government also gives premium subsidies for lower-income and middle-income households.
In Japan, funding for its mandatory national long-term care insurance is shared, with half being premiums paid by citizens and half being tax-funded.
The dialogue was part of the National Conference on Ageing 2026 (NCA 2026), which was organised by Universiti Putra Malaysia’s Malaysian Research Institute on Ageing (MyAgeing) together with Retirement Fund Inc (KWAP), the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) and Kendana.

Title: Off the trail, into danger: Mount Kinabalu guides warn trespassers of the price rescuers pay
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 2 — Security controls at Kinabalu Park are adequate, but trespassing on prohibited trails on Mount Kinabalu puts mountain guides at risk of physical injury and adds to the burden of search and rescue (SAR) operations.
Kinabalu Mountain Guides Association chairman Danson Bulangai said restricted areas had been marked with red paint along the park boundaries, with warning signs and references to the relevant legal provisions at every sub-station to deter trespassing.
“Using unauthorised trails endangers both mountain guides and the individuals involved, who face risks including physical injury, exposure to extreme weather and altitude sickness.
“Mountain guides also have to balance SAR duties with their primary responsibility of accompanying registered climbers, but we are always ready to assist whenever an incident requires SAR operations,” he told Bernama.
He said the vast area covered by Kinabalu Park, spanning about 754 square kilometres, posed a major challenge for the authorities and mountain guides in monitoring all potential routes.
Danson stressed that trespassing incidents created the wrong perception that mountain guides’ supervision was lax, despite the association having 241 registered guides, which he said were sufficient to meet the needs of official climbing activities.
He said the standard ratio for registered climbs was one guide for every five climbers, increasing to two guides for the same number of climbers if participants were under 16.
“The number of mountain guides also takes into account several other factors, including demand for specialised guiding services,” said Danson, who has worked in the sector since 2005.
He said mountain guides also paid close attention to the use of guide ropes, which were normally kept at a standard distance of three metres from climbers to prevent accidents at high altitudes.
However, the distance was reduced to less than one metre in thick fog to prevent climbers from straying from the actual trail.
“The situation becomes more challenging when white quartz veins on the granite surface resemble guide ropes, potentially confusing climbers when visibility is limited,” he said.
He said the association was actively strengthening emergency response skills through joint training with Sabah Parks (TTS) and the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), particularly in rope rescue techniques.
The rescue skills programme is planned to be extended to all association members in stages in the future.
The association also welcomed the planned requirement for every mountain guide to carry a walkie-talkie once repairs to the repeater system at the Panalaban sub-station were completed.
The measures followed previous incidents involving foreign trespassers, including Croatian climber Mauro Persic, 46, who was fined the maximum RM25,000 after falling and sustaining injuries to his ribs and legs while using an unauthorised trail last September. — Bernama

Title: Online renewal for 10-year Malaysian passports starts tomorrow
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 1 — Passport renewal services through the MyOnline Passport system will offer a choice of five- or 10-year validity periods starting tomorrow.
The Malaysian Immigration Department (JIM), in a Facebook post, said the new facility allows applicants to choose the passport validity period according to their respective needs.
“This initiative provides greater flexibility and convenience for Malaysians to choose the passport validity period according to their respective needs,” according to JIM. — Bernama

Title: Selangor schools open as usual tomorrow but parents may keep children home if concerned over haze, says state education dept
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 1 — All schools in Selangor will operate as usual tomorrow, according to the Selangor Education Department (JPN).
In a statement today, the department urged all parties to continue prioritising the health and safety of students and school personnel in view of the current haze situation.
“Students attending school are encouraged to wear face masks as a precautionary measure, particularly those who are sensitive to haze conditions.
“Schools, parents and guardians are also advised to remain alert to developments in air quality and comply with instructions and precautionary measures issued by the authorities,” it said.
However, parents or guardians who are concerned about their children’s health are allowed to keep them at home but must inform the school accordingly.
Any further updates will be communicated through the department’s and schools’ official channels to ensure that the public receives accurate and up-to-date information. — Bernama

Title: Over 400 people detained in drug raid on Jalan Sultan Ismail entertainment centre
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — A total of 417 individuals were detained after an unlicensed entertainment centre, suspected to be a hub for drug activities, was raided by the police early this morning on Jalan Sultan Ismail here.
Dang Wangi district police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said all the arrests in the raid, which started around 2.30am, consisted of premises guards, workers and visitors, including four Bangladeshi nationals.
“The raid was conducted following information that the entertainment premises was linked to drug abuse activities.
“All those detained were brought to the Dang Wangi district police headquarters (IPD) for documentation and urine screening tests,” he said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, in a separate raid, the police arrested eight individuals, including six foreigners, at another unlicensed entertainment centre on Jalan Tun Razak, around 2am earlier today.
Wangsa Maju IPD chief ACP Annas Sulaiman said the ‘Op Noda’ raid was carried out by a team of officers and members from the Anti-Vice, Gambling and Secret Societies Division (D7), along with the Wangsa Maju IPD Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID).
“Eight men who were arrested were aged between 21 and 40 years, including six foreigners, namely two each from Bangladesh and Myanmar who did not have valid travel documents, as well as two from China,” he also said.
Annas added that the police also seized various audio system equipment including two Pioneer brand DJ Multi Players, microphones, speakers, amplifiers, four bottles of various brands of liquor, and business sales receipts estimated to be worth more than RM2,100.
It was said that all arrests and seized items were brought to the Wangsa Maju IPD and the cases were investigated under Section 4(1) of the Federal Territory Entertainment Act, Section 6(1)(c) and Section 39(b) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, Regulation 25 of the National Registration Regulations 1990, and Section 186 of the Penal Code for obstructing public servants. — Bernama

Title: Man, 42, dies after collapsing during running event in Putrajaya
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 1 — A 42-year-old man died while participating in a running event here early this morning.
Putrajaya district police chief ACP Aidi Sham Mohamed said the victim was reported to have collapsed while participating in the event before being taken to the Putrajaya Hospital’s emergency department at around 6.52am.
“The Putrajaya Hospital authorities tried to resuscitate the victim, but their efforts were unsuccessful and the victim was pronounced dead at 6.54am.
“The initial investigation found that the deceased had no history of illness,” he also said.
He added that a post-mortem will be carried out to identify the cause of death. — Bernama

Title: Guar Chempedak assemblyman, son injured after SUV overturns in Yan crash
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Nov 1 — Guar Chempedak state assemblyman Abdul Ghafar Saad and his son sustained minor injuries after the sports utility vehicle (SUV) they were travelling in collided with a car in Ulu Sedaka, near Yan, yesterday.
Yan deputy district police chief DSP Aikap Dunding said police received information about the accident, which happened in front of Sekolah Kebangsaan Ulu Sedaka, at 8.41am.
“In the incident, the Proton X50 they were travelling in reportedly overturned after colliding with a Perodua Myvi,” he said in a statement today.
He said the Proton X50 SUV was driven by the 32-year-old son of the Guar Chempedak assemblyman, while Abdul Ghafar was a passenger in the vehicle.
“They sustained minor injuries, as did the driver of the Perodua Myvi,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Campaign ‘flag war’ begins in Melaka as parties stretch limited election budgets
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 1 — The excitement surrounding the 16th Melaka State Election is beginning to build, with a “flag war” among political parties visible along roadsides and in public hotspots following the completion of the nomination process yesterday.
A Bernama survey today found that political party flags had been put up in urban areas such as Kota Laksamana, Banda Hilir, Semabok, Duyong, Bukit Katil and Ayer Molek, featuring flags of Pakatan Harapan (PH), Barisan Nasional (BN), Perikatan Nasional (PN), Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) and Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu).
Several political parties are reusing flags from previous state elections in Johor and Negeri Sembilan for the Melaka polls.
Political party flags line the roads in Tanjung Bidara, Alor Gajah, ahead of the 16th Melaka state election on October 31, 2026. — Bernama pic
Melaka DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong said most of the flags were still in good condition, making their reuse a cost-saving measure to reduce expenses for the Melaka state election.
“We do not have a lot of financial resources, but putting up campaign materials such as flags, posters and banners is important to inform voters in a particular area that PH is contesting there.
“These campaign materials are also intended to introduce to voters the candidates representing PH… the main purpose is to convey that message, rather than compete over who puts up the most flags,” he told Bernama today.
Political party flags are being put up along roads in Tanjung Bidara, Alor Gajah, ahead of the 16th Melaka state election on October 31, 2026. — Bernama pic
He said the installation of PH flags, particularly in areas contested by DAP, was being carried out in stages, especially at locations frequented by the public.
He said about 2,000 flags would be put up in each state constituency contested by the party, with the number to be increased if necessary.
“We will also put up billboards and buntings. We started after the nomination process ended yesterday, and the work is still ongoing. The installation of billboards and buntings will be based on polling district areas and according to need,” he said.
Meanwhile, BN candidate for the Duyong state seat Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem said the flags displayed around the constituency had also been obtained from friends in Negeri Sembilan and Johor, where the respective state elections had concluded.
“Since Melaka is the third state to hold a state election, we are using whatever flags are available, as our budget is not large,” he said.
He said the installation of flags in the Duyong constituency was still being carried out in stages and was expected to be completed within the next two or three days.
A total of 79 candidates will contest 28 state seats in the 16th Melaka state election following the close of nominations yesterday.
Early voting is scheduled for November 10, while polling day will be held on November 14.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit the Bernama Melaka State Election Portal. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi: Three more Asean countries keen to join Malaysia-led children’s online safety push
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 1 — Thailand, Brunei and Cambodia are the latest Asean countries to have expressed interest in joining Malaysia, Indonesia and Singapore in efforts to address online safety issues involving children.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said he welcomed the development, describing it as a sign that Asean was moving in the same direction.
“In discussions with my counterparts from Indonesia and Singapore, we were already on the same page on this matter. So, this is even better as Southeast Asia will now move in the same direction because we will be stronger when we stand united, especially in dealing with major social media platforms.
“We believe this will help considerably, particularly as these platforms view the region as a single market. So, if the entire or majority of the Southeast Asian market starts speaking about the same issues, then it will be easier,” he said.
Fahmi was speaking at a press conference after attending the Safe Internet Campaign Programme at Multimedia University (MMU), Melaka Campus in Bukit Beruang here today.
Also present was Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah.
Elaborating on the joint efforts to address children’s online safety issues, Fahmi said Malaysia was also drawing lessons from the way certain restrictions had been implemented in other countries, such as Australia.
“We are also following and taking note of several recent cases in the US, in New Mexico, and this is very helpful in enabling us to take action or plan our next steps,” he said.
Fahmi was previously reported as saying that Malaysia and Indonesia had agreed to establish inter-agency cooperation at the implementation level to address children’s online safety issues, with plans also underway to involve Singapore.
On the Safe Internet Campaign, Fahmi said the programme had so far reached schools throughout Malaysia, with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) continuing to enhance its content from time to time. — Bernama

Title: BN banks on five-year track record to win fence-sitters at Melaka polls
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 1 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is confident that the achievements and performance of the state administration over the past five years will be among the key factors considered by fence-sitters in determining their choice of candidate in the Melaka state election on November 14.
Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said these voters would assess the party based on its ability to administer the state, as well as the effectiveness of policies and initiatives that directly benefit the people.
“Fence-sitters look at the direction of a party that will be given the mandate to administer a state or country.
“So they will look at what we have delivered to the people while administering the state before making their choice,” he told reporters after inspecting the preparations of the BN election machinery at the Telok Mas state constituency operations room here today.
Ab Rauf, who is also Chief Minister, said approaches taken by the state government to win over the group included the Wakil Rakyat Untuk Rakyat (WRUR), Hari Exco Bertemu Rakyat and Jelajah Ketua Menteri Sayang Rakyat programmes, which focus on identifying and resolving various issues faced by the people.
He said the implementation of the initiatives demonstrated the state government’s commitment to ensuring that every plan and policy was translated into action that benefits the community.
Ab Rauf said that through the WRUR programme, the state government had resolved about 75 per cent of the 4,800 complaints received involving various needs and issues faced by the community.
He said the achievement was among the results of efforts undertaken well before the election.
“We have done the work early so that the people are not sweet-talked during the 14-day campaign period. This is important because we must regard our position as elected representatives... as an opportunity to serve the people, not for the people to serve us,” he said.
Ab Rauf said among the elements frequently assessed by fence-sitters was the ability of each candidate elected as a people’s representative to understand the pulse of the community, including listening to and identifying their problems and needs.
“First, a people’s representative must be one of the people before becoming their representative. They must know the people’s problems, know their needs, listen to what they say and convey it to me so that I can formulate policies that the government can implement in the future,” he said.
Ab Rauf said BN left it to the people to assess all the efforts undertaken by the state government before deciding on their mandate on polling day.
“I hope what we have done and what we have delivered will be the best measure for them to continue working together with us in managing Melaka,” he said.
The Election Commission has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka polls, while early voting will be held on November 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Melaka polls: MCMC won’t interfere in parties’ social media campaigns, will only act on complaints
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 1 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will not interfere in social media campaigns by contesting political parties during the 16th Melaka State Election, says Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
Instead, he said the commission will actively monitor social media platforms and only initiate investigations or take action against posts upon receiving complaints from the public.
“To date, these are the only two mechanisms MCMC will apply to posts concerning campaigning by contesting parties on social media platforms,” he said when asked about MCMC’s online monitoring measures during the Melaka polls scheduled for November 14.
Fahmi said this at a press conference after attending the Safe Internet Programme at the Multimedia University (MMU) Melaka Campus in Bukit Beruang here today.
Elaborating, Fahmi said MCMC is also monitoring the misuse of social media accounts to spread false information, the use of deepfakes, and extremely offensive content.
“We are also tracking a trend where content is uploaded by fake accounts, which then disappear once the post is published. This happens frequently and is not something we only anticipate during the state election; it is being detected more often and is quite worrying.
“We found that much of the content containing derogatory statements against the King originated from overseas-based accounts. Upon closer examination, we found that most of them, or 98 per cent, were fake accounts, so we take this very seriously,” he said.
Asked about Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) decision to name Parti Amanah Negara vice-president Adly Zahari as its Chief Minister candidate, Fahmi said it was due to his experience.
“He is an experienced figure. He has served as a state assemblyman for two terms and was previously Chief Minister,” said Fahmi, who is also PH communications director.
PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari was previously reported as saying that Adly, who is the coalition’s candidate for the Bukit Katil state constituency, was chosen as the poster boy and Chief Minister candidate should the coalition win the Melaka polls.
The Election Commission (EC) has set November 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka State Election, with early voting on November 10.
For the latest news on the election, visit [https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/](https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/?utm_source=chatgpt.com). — Bernama

Title: Anwar among racing buffs in Sepang to watch Marquez win Malaysian MotoGP
Article:
SEPANG, Nov 1 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today spent time watching the 2026 Malaysian Motorcycle Grand Prix (GP) race at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) here.
Anwar’s arrival was welcomed by Minister of Youth and Sports Dr. Mohammed Taufiq Johari and SIC Chief Executive Officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif.
He was then brought to tour the K2 Hillstand spectator seating area before heading to the starting grid to mingle with spectators ahead of the MotoGP class race, which began at 3pm.
The atmosphere at the racing circuit was further enlightened by a rendition of the national anthem, Negaraku, by National Songstress Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza Tarudin.
Today’s race saw Ducati Lenovo Team rider Marc Marquez strengthen his position at the summit of the 2026 MotoGP world championship after emerging as the champion, followed by Pedro Acosta of Red Bull KTM Factory Racing in second place and Alex Marquez of BK8 Gresini Racing MotoGP in third.
The victory saw Marc Marquez collect 399 points, thereby widening the gap to 44 points over his closest challenger, Jorge Martin of Aprilia Racing, who now has 355 points. — Bernama

Title: Azalina: All 218 MPs get a role in reforms under CSA as AG-PP split, PM term limit need cross-party support
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — Cross-party cooperation through the Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) is important in building parliamentary consensus to advance institutional reforms in the country, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
In this regard, she welcomed Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s support for the implementation of the CSA, as well as his proposal to extend the cooperation to more opposition parties.
She said political differences should not be an obstacle to cooperation for the sake of national stability and the interests of the people, adding that the approach would also provide an avenue for all the existing 218 MPs to play a role in the parliamentary democratic process.
“This is to ensure that the voices of the people represented by their respective Members of Parliament are also involved in determining the direction and future of national institutions through debates and voting in Parliament,” she said in a Facebook post today.
Azalina said the reforms include separating the roles of the Attorney General and the Public Prosecutor, as well as a proposal to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure to 10 years, which require cross-party scrutiny and support as they involve the national interest and amendments to the Federal Constitution.
She said a similar approach to cooperation had previously been implemented when Umno was part of the federal government during the previous term.
Azalina said that as part of the Unity Government, Barisan Nasional (BN) would continue to play a constructive role in maintaining political stability, strengthening democratic institutions and ensuring the country’s administration functions effectively in the interests of the people.
Yesterday, Ahmad Zahid, who is also BN chairman, described the CSA as a positive development in addressing and resolving issues affecting the people.
Last Thursday, the Madani Government signed a CSA with six Bersatu MPs led by its president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, as well as seven other MPs, including Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman.
On the same day, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that the agreement was aimed at ensuring the continuity of the government’s administration and the effective implementation of the country’s development agenda, including Budget 2027, in the interests of the people. — Bernama

Title: Zahid: Rural and Regional Development Ministry aims to clear RM259.5m in project arrears by year-end
Article:
BAGAN DATUK, Nov 1 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi hopes that outstanding payments for projects under the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) can be resolved amicably by the end of this year.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, said efforts would be made to ensure payments for completed projects that had yet to be settled, including progress payments due to contractors and suppliers, could be made.
“We will endeavour to ensure that funds are made available to settle payments for projects that have been completed but remain unpaid, as well as progress payments due to contractors and suppliers.
“I have explained this matter in Parliament, and it was also answered by the Finance Minister II.
“I hope it can be resolved amicably,” he told a press conference after attending the 2026 Deepavali Santunan Kasih event at the Bagan Datuk Umno Hall here today.
Ahmad Zahid was asked to comment on a video uploaded on TikTok by his press secretary Fadzmel Fadzil, concerning allegations of delayed payments for projects amounting to more than RM200 million.
On October 30, it was reported that outstanding interim payments to contractors and compensation to landowners totalled about RM259.5 million as at September 30, involving 112 projects. — Bernama

Title: BN ready to invite Perikatan to join state govt if it wins Melaka polls, says Zahid
Article:
BAGAN DATUK, Nov 1 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is prepared to invite Perikatan Nasional (PN) to join the state administration if the coalition succeeds in forming the government in the 16th Melaka State Election on November 14.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the approach was taken to respect the people’s mandate and the political understanding reached between the two coalitions, similar to what had previously been implemented in Negeri Sembilan.
“As happened in Negeri Sembilan, when the government was formed, we honoured the appointments to ensure that they (PN) were part of the government. The same happened in Melaka when the previous Unity Government was formed, with our partners in PH (Pakatan Harapan) also appointed as state executive councillors (Exco) and deputy Exco members, but they subsequently decided to leave.
“So we will do the same for PN assemblymen who win their respective seats and, God willing, if we form the government, we will also invite them to be part of the state government,” he told a press conference after attending the 2026 Deepavali Santunan Kasih event at Dewan Umno Bagan Datuk here today.
In this election, BN is contesting 23 of the 28 seats up for grabs, while PN is contesting five seats.
The Election Commission has set November 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, while early voting will take place on November 10.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka state election, visit
https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026
. — Bernama

Title: Four dead as cars veer into oncoming lanes in separate KL, Johor crashes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — Four people were killed in two separate road accidents involving four vehicles in Kuala Lumpur and Kulai, Johor, with both crashes believed to have occurred after cars veered into oncoming lanes.
In an accident involving a Perodua Myvi and a Toyota Vellfire at Kilometer 23 of the Middle Ring Road 2 (MRR2), near Bukit Antarabangsa, early this morning, two men were killed.
Ampang Jaya district police Chief ACP Khairul Anuar Khalid said in the 12.40am incident, the Myvi, which was travelling from Taman Melawati towards Cheras, is believed to have lost control before skidding into the opposite lane.
He said the vehicle then collided with the front of the Vellfire travelling in the opposite direction.
“The Myvi driver sustained serious head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene by medical personnel from Ampang Hospital,” he said in a statement today.
He said the Vellfire driver and a passenger were also injured and rushed to Ampang Hospital; however, the driver was pronounced dead while receiving treatment at the hospital, while the passenger remains hospitalised.
Khairul Anuar said the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He urged witnesses to come forward to assist in the investigation by contacting the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division at the Ampang Jaya district police headquarters.
A video showing the aftermath of the accident had earlier gone viral on social media.
Meanwhile, in Kulai, a mother and her daughter were killed in an accident involving two vehicles at Jalan Senai-Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Senai here yesterday.
Kulai district police chief ACP Tan Seng Lee said police received information about the accident involving a Toyota Vios and a Mazda at about 2.30pm.
He said the accident is believed to have occurred when the Mazda, driven by a 30-year-old woman with her 69-year-old mother as a passenger, skidded into the opposite lane.
“The accident left the Mazda driver seriously injured. She was pronounced dead while receiving treatment at Temenggong Seri Maharaja Tun Ibrahim Hospital, while her mother died at Sultanah Aminah Hospital.
“However, the 30-year-old male driver of the Toyota Vios sustained only minor injuries. The actual cause of the accident is still under investigation,” he said in a statement today.
Tan said the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Members of the public with information about the accident can contact the Kulai district police headquarters Traffic Division or the investigating officer, Inspector Ahmad Safuan Abu Naim, at 017-7573507 to assist the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak explores collaboration with Russia on rocket, satellite launches, says Abang Johari
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 1 — The Sarawak government is exploring potential collaboration with Russia in rocket and satellite launches, leveraging the state’s strategic location near the Equator.
Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg said the proposal was raised by the Ambassador of the Russian Federation to Malaysia, Naiyl M. Latypov, during a courtesy call last week.
“I mentioned that we (Sarawak) require more engineers and are prepared to explore collaboration to develop a larger pool of professionals in the field,” he said at the inauguration of the extension building of Gurdwara Sahib Kuching here today.
Abang Johari said Sarawak must capitalise on growing international interest in the state by implementing effective policies and ensuring clear development plans.
Recently, local media reported that Russia had expressed its readiness to discuss potential collaboration with Sarawak in various sectors, including aerospace, energy, agriculture, shipbuilding and education. — Bernama

Title: AGC files appeal, weighs bid to reinstate murder charge against senior Perak cop in student hit-and-run case
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Nov 1 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) is considering whether to seek the reinstatement of a murder charge against a senior police officer in the case involving the death of student Muhammad Zaharif Affendi Muhd Zamrie, following the officer’s conviction on a lesser charge of causing death.
Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar said the AGC had filed an appeal at the Court of Appeal last week against the Ipoh High Court’s decision, but was still examining the various aspects of the case before deciding on the arguments to be submitted.
He said he had discussed the matter with AGC Prosecution Division head Datuk Masri Mohd Daud and the head of its Trial and Appeals Division.
“We want to examine every aspect of this case, including whether we should submit arguments for the original murder charge to be reinstated, or take any other appropriate action based on the circumstances of the case and the court’s decision,” he said.
Mohd Dusuki was speaking to reporters after attending the launch of the Attorney-General’s Chambers Madani Adopted School programme at Sekolah Kebangsaan Pasir Hor here today.
Asked whether the AGC had identified any gaps or shortcomings in the High Court’s decision, Mohd Dusuki said it was too early to comment as the prosecution had yet to receive the full grounds of judgment.
On October 28, the Ipoh High Court sentenced DSP Mohd Nazri Abdul Razak, 47, to seven years and six months’ imprisonment after he pleaded guilty to an amended charge of causing the death of Muhammad Zaharif, three years ago.
The charge was amended from murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code to one under Section 304(b), which carries a maximum jail term of 10 years, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
The judge ordered Mohd Nazri to serve his sentence from December 15, 2023, the date of his arrest. He was also ordered to pay RM50,000 in compensation to the victim’s father, Muhd Zamrie Zainal Abidin, 58, or face an additional year in prison if he failed to do so.
Mohd Nazri was accused of causing the death of Muhammad Zaharif, 17, near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Jati in Ipoh between 11.55am and 12.32pm on December 15, 2023.
He was initially charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years and at least 12 strokes of the cane upon conviction. — Bernama

Title: Brace for the toughest GE yet: Loke warns DAP as BN and Perikatan close ranks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 1 — DAP must prepare for its toughest general election yet as growing cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) threatens to upend the country’s political landscape, Anthony Loke said today.
The DAP secretary-general warned that recent political pacts struck between the two coalitions across Johor, Negeri Sembilan, and Melaka present a serious challenge to DAP and its Pakatan Harapan (PH) partners, NST reported.
Addressing delegates at the Kuala Lumpur Federal Territories DAP annual convention today, Loke urged members to cast aside complacency and tighten the party’s machinery ahead of the 16th general election (GE16).
“Whatever their political calculations, the most important thing is that our party must remain united and strengthen ourselves together with our partners in Pakatan Harapan,” he said.
With the convention likely serving as the party’s final annual gathering in the capital before GE16, Loke called on members to ramp up ground preparations and prioritise defending their parliamentary seats. DAP’s core objective in Kuala Lumpur remains retaining all five parliamentary seats secured during the 15th general election (GE15).
“Kuala Lumpur DAP must help the party defend all five seats that we won in GE15,” he said. PH currently holds 10 of the 11 parliamentary seats across the Federal Territories.
Loke stressed that public support can no longer be taken for granted, citing the party’s recent electoral drubbings as a critical wake-up call.
DAP reassessed its ground strategy after a devastating wipeout in the November 2025 Sabah state election, where it lost all eight contested seats, including six traditional strongholds.
State poll wake-up calls
The electoral tremors continued into earlier state contests. In the July Johor election, DAP secured only six of the 17 seats it contested, surrendering four previously held constituencies.
In August, the party took nine of 11 seats in Negeri Sembilan, but suffered a high-profile casualty when Loke himself lost the Chennah state seat to MCA’s Siow Kong Choon by 688 votes.
Loke confirmed that DAP conducted an extensive post-mortem to address systemic weaknesses uncovered during those defeats, noting that those hard lessons must dictate future campaign strategy.
“The challenges we face are becoming greater as we approach the next election,” he warned.
Beyond the ballot box, Loke acknowledged that party leaders have become frequent targets of political attacks and viral satire online.
While accepting that criticism comes with the territory of holding federal power, he insisted members must stay focused on public delivery rather than retreating into defensiveness.
Acknowledging federal administrative shortcomings, Loke urged leaders to proactively communicate the coalition’s tangible reforms to the electorate.
He noted that doing the right thing does not always bring immediate political dividends, but leaders cannot abandon their core duties under the weight of electoral pressure.

Title: Immigration Dept: Report special pass irregularities directly to us or MACC
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 1 — The Immigration Department (JIM) has urged the public to report alleged irregularities in the issuance of Special Passes involving its officers in Kuala Lumpur directly to the authorities.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said information or evidence could be submitted to JIM or the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) to facilitate a comprehensive investigation.
“Providing information directly to the authorities is crucial to protecting the confidentiality of information and preserving the integrity of evidence.
“Publicly disclosing information about suspected unlawful activities before reporting it to the authorities could prompt those involved to halt their activities, change their modus operandi or destroy evidence, thereby hindering investigations and enforcement action,” he said in a statement today.
Zakaria said JIM welcomed information on alleged misconduct by its officers and would ensure that all reports received were reviewed and referred for appropriate action under the prevailing laws and regulations.
He said the department viewed the allegations seriously and would not tolerate misconduct, abuse of power or breaches of integrity by its officers, regardless of rank or position.
As part of efforts to strengthen integrity and accountability, Zakaria said a total of 849 immigration officers had faced disciplinary action from 2023 to October this year, including 73 who were dismissed.
From January to October this year alone, 96 officers faced disciplinary action, including 18 who were dismissed.
He said the figures reflected the department’s firm stance on taking action against officers found to have committed disciplinary offences.
JIM would continue to strengthen integrity, procedural compliance and internal controls to ensure that all services were delivered transparently and in accordance with the law, he added. — Bernama
